# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Welcome to our interactive grassroots newsletter. As we approach the Midterm Election 2026, this newsletter is dedicated to keeping the hardworking constituents of Illinois' 6th Congressional District informed and engaged.

Our campaign is built on a "district-first" mentality. We are committed to prioritizing your needs, focusing on fundamental ideals of sensible solutions and open dialogue. Through this newsletter, we will provide you with regular updates on policy, campaign events, and current community events happening right here in our district.
Click the button below to make a donation today. Your donations are what makes this possible.
---
| | [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/4OmPgi_hm7K?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)
---
| |
---
| |
## Kitchen Table Tuesday.
The Conforti Brief.
District-First Events.
---
| |
### Educate. Inform. Invite.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | Wasteful spending in government is too often viewed as "lining the pockets of special interest groups" while neglecting hardworking families. Local governments in Illinois have become the **hallmarks of this wasteful spending that forgets about everyday, hardworking families.** To combat this, my goal is to push for strict spending caps to limit the amount added to the national debt. When in Washington, I will push for these spending caps to limit the debt we incur to pay for radical spending agendas.
. More spending inevitably leads to more taxes. By curbing government spending, we can stop the cycle of tax increases on working families. I will **work to curb the spending in Washington, D.C., and put an end to the tax hikes on our working families.** We must prioritize fiscal responsibility to ensure Illinoisans are no longer overburdened by a high tax agenda - an agenda that has seen people fleeing Illinois.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | **Demanding Real Healthcare Transparency**
.A recent survey by the Commonwealth Fund, as reported by the Association of Health Care Journalists (AHCJ), underscores a crisis that families across our district know all too well: **health care and health insurance are unaffordable for many Americans.**
.When consumers cannot afford insurance or care, they are more likely to skip needed doctor and emergency room visits, placing their health at serious risk. This is an unacceptable reality. The survey found that a staggering 42% of respondents cited high insurance premiums as the most important health care problem, while 36% pointed to high out-of-pocket costs.
.This financial strain is only compounding the challenges hardworking families face. As the Urban Institute notes, the high costs of necessities like electricity, food, housing, heating fuel, and gasoline are already **stretching budgets to the breaking point.**
.Unfortunately, the policies of Democrats like Sean Casten have consistently failed the residents of Illinois' 6th District when it comes to healthcare affordability. **Democrat-championed policies like Obamacare have been a disaster for Illinois, causing healthcare costs to rise steadily over the last decade.** Today, many counties only have two options for consumers, making the ironically named Affordable Care Act entirely unaffordable for most families and small businesses.
.It is clear that the current system is failing us, and costs are projected to keep rising. Employers' health plan medical costs are expected to rise by 9% in 2027, among the highest increases in nearly two decades. When the costs of care rise, employers inevitably shift more of those expenses to workers through higher deductibles and narrower networks.
.Niki Conforti plans to help the residents of the 6th District by bringing her invaluable professional experience as a former healthcare director to Congress. Once in office, **Niki will fight to make healthcare more accessible and affordable** through initiatives like these:
.
* **Fostering Market Competition:** By demanding true transparency in medical billing, Niki aims to drive up competition among healthcare systems. This competition will lower prices and drive down out-of-pocket costs for families and small business owners.
.
* **Expanding Consumer Choice:** Niki believes that consumers should have more options in the marketplace and that policies should be transportable across state lines.
.

It's time for sensible solutions that **provide real relief**. We must replace a broken system with one that empowers patients, fosters competition, and delivers true affordability.
.
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/wj43KAkj1HF?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# District-First
# Events
---
| | **Inviting voters** to community events and how they can get involved!**
****Plant a sign in your yard today** and watch our grassroots movement grow!
---
| |
---
| | **Show Your Support: Request a Yard Sign Today!**
.As we approach the November 3rd General Election, grassroots engagement is essential to defeating incumbent Sean Casten. You can help spread the word and showcase our "district-first" mentality by placing a Niki Conforti yard sign in your yard. **Visible community support is a powerful way to show your neighbors that we are united** in the fight for economic affordability, community safety, and sensible solutions for the 6th District.
.To request a sign for your home or business, please contact our team at [**info@conforti4congress.com.**](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Requesting%20a%20Yard%20Sign&body=) Strong local momentum is the key to curbing reckless spending and securing a safer future for Illinois families.
.
Let us know you would like a sign, and we will arrange to get one to you right away!.
.
.
**Key Dates for the 2026 General Election (DuPage County)**
* First day to apply for a vote-by-mail ballot:**August 5th**
* Early voting and vote-by-mail voting begins: **September 24th**
* Last day to request a vote-by-mail ballot: **October 29th**
* Last day for early voting: **November 2nd**
* General Election Day:**November 3rd**
.

**Key Dates for the 2026 General Election (Cook County)**
* First day to apply for a vote-by-mail ballot: **August 5th**
* First day to vote early in Chicago (Downtown Only): **September 24th** Last day for online voter registration: **October 18th**
* Early voting opens in all 50 city wards and suburban Cook County: **October 19th**
* Deadline for vote-by-mail applications: **October 29th**
* General Election Day: **November 3rd**
.

**Get out the vote:** whether you plan to vote by mail, early voting in person, or voting in person on election day, it’s important we get out the vote to defeat incumbent Sean Casten.

| That premise challenges a hierarchy that museums helped construct. | |
---
| Feature · Museums & Visual Culture
---
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opens in Los Angeles Today — Putting Comics, Cinema, Illustration, Painting and Popular Images Under One Roof to Make a Bigger Argument About What Museums Decide Is Worth Remembering
Tuesday the 22nd of September 2026 marks the public opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles’s Exposition Park. Founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson, the museum occupies a 300,000-square-foot building designed by Ma Yansong of MAD with Stantec, surrounded by a 13-acre landscape designed by Mia Lehrer and Studio-MLA. Inside are more than 100,000 square feet of exhibition space across more than thirty galleries. But the scale is not the most consequential part of the opening. The museum’s larger proposition is curatorial: illustration, comics, murals, cinema, painting, photography and popular visual culture can be read as parts of the same long human tradition of telling stories through images.
|
---
That premise challenges a hierarchy that museums helped construct. Fine-art institutions have traditionally given painting and sculpture a different cultural status from commercial illustration, comic art, concept design and cinematic objects. The Lucas Museum deliberately collapses some of those distinctions. Works associated with Artemisia Gentileschi, Norman Rockwell, Frida Kahlo, Robert Colescott and Diego Rivera can exist within the same institutional framework as underground comics, children’s-book illustration, film design and material from the Lucas Archives.
The inaugural exhibitions make that ambition unusually explicit. More than 1,300 works trace narrative art across cultures and centuries, while dedicated galleries address mythology, family, community, sports, murals and cinema. Star Wars in Motion presents designs, props, costumes and illustrations connected to movement and vehicles across the first six Star Wars films. The museum therefore moves constantly between objects normally separated by department, market and audience.
| | In their words
---
The artists in this collection didn’t just create images, they connected our modern imaginations with our ancient emotions.
— George Lucas, co-founder of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
The building itself extends the argument. Ma Yansong conceived its curving form as an emotional environment rather than a neutral container. A central arch spans 185 feet above a public plaza, while more than 1,200 individually shaped exterior panels create the continuous surface. Before a visitor sees a collection object, the building has already announced that entering a museum can be part of a narrative experience.
| |
---
What the new museum is arguing
| | 01
---
The collection
More than 40,000 works and extensive archives bring painting, illustration, comics, murals, photography and cinema into a collection organised around visual storytelling rather than a single traditional medium.
| 02
---
The building
Ma Yansong’s 300,000-square-foot structure contains more than 100,000 square feet of galleries and sits inside a new 13-acre park in Exposition Park.
| 03
---
The hierarchy
By placing popular and commercial image-making beside established fine art, the museum asks whether the cultural importance of an image depends on the category in which museums historically placed it.
That question arrives at a useful moment. Contemporary audiences encounter images without respecting institutional boundaries. A Renaissance painting, a movie still, a comic panel and an illustration can all appear on the same screen within seconds. Digital culture has flattened distribution even when the art market and museum world retain older hierarchies of value. The Lucas Museum responds to an audience already accustomed to moving rapidly between visual languages.
The risk is equally clear. A category as broad as narrative art can become so inclusive that it loses analytical precision. Museums create meaning partly by drawing distinctions, and putting many forms together does not automatically explain their different histories or social functions. The success of the institution will therefore depend on whether its galleries can preserve those differences while still making the larger connections convincing.
| The Lucas Museum opens today with an argument larger than Star Wars and larger than George Lucas’s own collecting history. It asks visitors to reconsider the invisible borders around visual culture: fine art and popular art, unique object and reproduced image, museum masterpiece and mass entertainment. Whether those borders disappear is less important than the fact that a major new institution has made questioning them its starting point.
---
| · · ·
---
| | By the numbers
---
1,300+
works from the museum’s collection appear across the inaugural exhibitions, spread through more than thirty galleries devoted to visual storytelling across cultures, periods and media.
The Lucas Museum opens to the public today in a 300,000-square-foot building on a 13-acre Los Angeles campus. Its permanent collection holds more than 40,000 works, while the institution also includes two theaters, a free research library, learning spaces and public gardens. The opening film programme begins today in both museum theaters.
| Also today · Painting
---
Nicole Eisenman Opens at the Royal Academy Today — Bringing Three Decades of Painting and Sculpture Into a London Survey of Bodies, Friendship, Politics, Humour and the Uneasy Experience of Living With Other People
A major exhibition devoted to Nicole Eisenman opens today, the 22nd of September, at the Royal Academy of Arts in London and runs into February 2027. Eisenman’s practice has moved between painting, drawing and sculpture while repeatedly returning to the social body: groups eating, drinking, waiting, protesting, relaxing or simply sharing space. The work can be comic, awkward, tender and grotesque within the same scene, borrowing freely from art history while remaining rooted in contemporary experience.
|
---
Eisenman’s group scenes are especially effective because they rarely present community as uncomplicated harmony. People can be physically close while psychologically elsewhere. Figures look at phones, turn away, slump, stare or occupy the same setting without necessarily sharing the same emotional reality. That ambiguity gives the work a recognisable contemporary texture.
A survey spanning roughly three decades also makes it possible to see how Eisenman’s recurring concerns survive changes in medium and context. Humour remains important, but it does not neutralise the seriousness of the work. Instead, comedy becomes a way of keeping social observation open-ended.
| |
---
At a glance
| | The opening
---
22 September 2026 · Royal Academy of Arts · London · exhibition running into February 2027
| The practice
---
Painting · drawing · sculpture · figurative scenes shaped by art history, humour, politics and contemporary social life
| The question
---
How can figurative art represent community without pretending that being together automatically means belonging together?
| · · ·
---
| Short note
---
Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre Turns Andrzej Wajda’s Cinema Into a Live Musical Event Tonight — Pairing Film Images With an Orchestra Performing Music by Penderecki, Komeda and Other Composers
Wajda – Music takes place tonight, the 22nd of September, at the Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre. The concert combines scenes from films by Andrzej Wajda with live orchestral performance under Adam Sztaba, drawing on music associated with composers including Krzysztof Penderecki and Krzysztof Komeda. By separating the score from its usual recorded form and restoring it as a live event, the programme asks audiences to hear familiar screen images differently.

clean_body: That premise challenges a hierarchy that museums helped construct. | | | | | | | | | ON AIR | | | | | 09 • 22 • 26 | That premise challenges a hierarchy that museums helped construct. | | | Feature · Museums & Visual Culture The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opens in Los Angeles Today — Putting Comics, Cinema, Illustration, Painting and Popular Images Under One Roof to Make a Bigger Argument About What Museums Decide Is Worth Remembering Tuesday the 22nd of September 2026 marks the public opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles’s Exposition Park. Founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson, the museum occupies a 300,000-square-foot building designed by Ma Yansong of MAD with Stantec, surrounded by a 13-acre landscape designed by Mia Lehrer and Studio-MLA. Inside are more than 100,000 square feet of exhibition space across more than thirty galleries. But the scale is not the most consequential part of the opening. The museum’s larger proposition is curatorial: illustration, comics, murals, cinema, painting, photography and popular visual culture can be read as parts of the same long human tradition of telling stories through images. | That premise challenges a hierarchy that museums helped construct. Fine-art institutions have traditionally given painting and sculpture a different cultural status from commercial illustration, comic art, concept design and cinematic objects. The Lucas Museum deliberately collapses some of those distinctions. Works associated with Artemisia Gentileschi, Norman Rockwell, Frida Kahlo, Robert Colescott and Diego Rivera can exist within the same institutional framework as underground comics, children’s-book illustration, film design and material from the Lucas Archives. The inaugural exhibitions make that ambition unusually explicit. More than 1,300 works trace narrative art across cultures and centuries, while dedicated galleries address mythology, family, community, sports, murals and cinema. Star Wars in Motion presents designs, props, costumes and illustrations connected to movement and vehicles across the first six Star Wars films. The museum therefore moves constantly between objects normally separated by department, market and audience. | | In their words The artists in this collection didn’t just create images, they connected our modern imaginations with our ancient emotions. — George Lucas, co-founder of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art The building itself extends the argument. Ma Yansong conceived its curving form as an emotional environment rather than a neutral container. A central arch spans 185 feet above a public plaza, while more than 1,200 individually shaped exterior panels create the continuous surface. Before a visitor sees a collection object, the building has already announced that entering a museum can be part of a narrative experience. | | What the new museum is arguing | | 01 The collection More than 40,000 works and extensive archives bring painting, illustration, comics, murals, photography and cinema into a collection organised around visual storytelling rather than a single traditional medium. | 02 The building Ma Yansong’s 300,000-square-foot structure contains more than 100,000 square feet of galleries and sits inside a new 13-acre park in Exposition Park. | 03 The hierarchy By placing popular and commercial image-making beside established fine art, the museum asks whether the cultural importance of an image depends on the category in which museums historically placed it. That question arrives at a useful moment. Contemporary audiences encounter images without respecting institutional boundaries. A Renaissance painting, a movie still, a comic panel and an illustration can all appear on the same screen within seconds. Digital culture has flattened distribution even when the art market and museum world retain older hierarchies of value. The Lucas Museum responds to an audience already accustomed to moving rapidly between visual languages. The risk is equally clear. A category as broad as narrative art can become so inclusive that it loses analytical precision. Museums create meaning partly by drawing distinctions, and putting many forms together does not automatically explain their different histories or social functions. The success of the institution will therefore depend on whether its galleries can preserve those differences while still making the larger connections convincing. | The Lucas Museum opens today with an argument larger than Star Wars and larger than George Lucas’s own collecting history. It asks visitors to reconsider the invisible borders around visual culture: fine art and popular art, unique object and reproduced image, museum masterpiece and mass entertainment. Whether those borders disappear is less important than the fact that a major new institution has made questioning them its starting point. | · · · | | By the numbers 1,300+ works from the museum’s collection appear across the inaugural exhibitions, spread through more than thirty galleries devoted to visual storytelling across cultures, periods and media. The Lucas Museum opens to the public today in a 300,000-square-foot building on a 13-acre Los Angeles campus. Its permanent collection holds more than 40,000 works, while the institution also includes two theaters, a free research library, learning spaces and public gardens. The opening film programme begins today in both museum theaters. | Also today · Painting Nicole Eisenman Opens at the Royal Academy Today — Bringing Three Decades of Painting and Sculpture Into a London Survey of Bodies, Friendship, Politics, Humour and the Uneasy Experience of Living With Other People A major exhibition devoted to Nicole Eisenman opens today, the 22nd of September, at the Royal Academy of Arts in London and runs into February 2027. Eisenman’s practice has moved between painting, drawing and sculpture while repeatedly returning to the social body: groups eating, drinking, waiting, protesting, relaxing or simply sharing space. The work can be comic, awkward, tender and grotesque within the same scene, borrowing freely from art history while remaining rooted in contemporary experience. | Eisenman’s group scenes are especially effective because they rarely present community as uncomplicated harmony. People can be physically close while psychologically elsewhere. Figures look at phones, turn away, slump, stare or occupy the same setting without necessarily sharing the same emotional reality. That ambiguity gives the work a recognisable contemporary texture. A survey spanning roughly three decades also makes it possible to see how Eisenman’s recurring concerns survive changes in medium and context. Humour remains important, but it does not neutralise the seriousness of the work. Instead, comedy becomes a way of keeping social observation open-ended. | | At a glance | | The opening 22 September 2026 · Royal Academy of Arts · London · exhibition running into February 2027 | The practice Painting · drawing · sculpture · figurative scenes shaped by art history, humour, politics and contemporary social life | The question How can figurative art represent community without pretending that being together automatically means belonging together? | · · · | Short note Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre Turns Andrzej Wajda’s Cinema Into a Live Musical Event Tonight — Pairing Film Images With an Orchestra Performing Music by Penderecki, Komeda and Other Composers Wajda – Music takes place tonight, the 22nd of September, at the Gdańsk Shakespeare Theatre. The concert combines scenes from films by Andrzej Wajda with live orchestral performance under Adam Sztaba, drawing on music associated with composers including Krzysztof Penderecki and Krzysztof Komeda. Dear Friend who has common sense,

I'm always going to stand with America.

I'm always going to reject the extremes.

I'm always going to reject Socialism.

I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.

And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and
even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and
anonymously attacking me.

This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of
the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.

But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the
Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party.

They want to...

Abolish our borders

Abolish the electoral college

Abolish Israel

Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in
the "DSA!" platform)

That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political
fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and
onto ballots across the country.

The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to
every day still aren't buying it.

I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:

71% of Americans reject socialism

67% of Democrat voters reject socialism

While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism

But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one
that looks the most powerful.

And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and
getting louder. The media is their megaphone.

Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really
do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies

Nothing could be further from the truth.

I'M STANDING UP TO THEM.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.

So, can I ask you a favor?

Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me
against the daily barrage of hit-pieces

IF YOU CAN DONATE JUST $25 IT WOULD BE A BIG HELP TO ME.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the
"real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around
the rest of America.

You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and
recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I
banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the
larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.

Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party
bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:

"FETTERMAN DRAWS SHADOW PRIMARY FROM DEMOCRATS EAGER TO REPLACE HIM:
THE PENNSYLVANIA SENATOR HAS LONG IRKED MEMBERS OF HIS OWN PARTY" ~
BLOOMBERG

If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not
backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense
and putting our country first.

Thank you!

John Fetterman

P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email
from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation
for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And
I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a
big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong
borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my
constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not
to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral
College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye
with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for
Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous
one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this
vision before it's too late. CAN I COUNT ON YOU TO STAND WITH ME
TODAY?

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Here's a difficult update:
body:
I’m turning to engaged supporters like you for help.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1402&source=&t=1&akid=3743%2E124072%2EJAclFd) | | | |

Peter, this update isn't great:
**1.** Stephen Miller went on Fox News to rant and rave about me, President Trump took to the GOP’s biggest stage to personally attack me last week, **and JD Vance came to North Carolina yesterday to spread lies about me and prop up my Republican opponent.**
**2.** By the latest tally, Republicans are pouring over $100 million into this race so far – and the Senate’s top GOP super PAC is live with false attack ads against me.
**3\. The GOP’s attacks are working: A new poll shows that this race is still statistically tied.**
The GOP is outspending us, and I need your help to fight back immediately so we can stay on track to flip this must-win seat.
My team asked me to reach out to engaged supporters like you, so I’m personally asking:
[**_Peter, will you make your first donation to my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina so we can flip this seat and the Senate majority? No matter how much you give, it all adds up fast when everyone pitches in._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1402&amount=5&t=8&akid=3743%2E124072%2EJAclFd)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

**Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire is actively recruiting patriots like you to volunteer to knock 100 doors before polls close on Election Day.**

That’s it. 100 doors.

We are 42 days away from Election Day, and **we are knocking 400,000 doors across New Hampshire** to build the Red Wall for generations to come.

Doors win wars, and the only way we'll make New Hampshire a Liberty State is by meeting voters where they are and mobilizing them to cast their ballots on Election Day.

**That’s why we need to commit to knocking just 100 doors around your community!**

### Can Philadelphia become America's next Mississippi Miracle?
For the first time, I'm sharing the official announcement for our **2nd Annual Conference** --this year, **The F3 Forum: Faith, Family & the Future of Education in America**--taking place **Saturday, October 24, 2026, in the heart of Germantown, Philadelphia.**
🎟️ **Registration is now open!**
**[REGISTER HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/569ce0f6-fd6b-4db0-97a7-4f5ec02c0bb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
**THE F3 FORUM: Faith • Family • the Future of Education in America**
**Can Philadelphia Become America 's Next Mississippi Miracle?**
**Saturday, October 24, 2026**
**9:00 a.m. -2:00 p.m.**
Doors open at 8:30 a.m.
**The Braid Mill**
441 E. High Street
Philadelphia, PA 19144
This isn't just another event.
It is a community-wide conversation about **literacy, opportunity, and student success --and what it will take to change the trajectory of Philadelphia's children.**
Last year, we gathered in Philadelphia for our inaugural Seed & Roots conference to focus on faith, family, and the future of work in America.
This year, we are taking the conversation directly into the community--and focusing on one of the most urgent issues confronting our families: **the education of our children.**
Mississippi accomplished what many believed was impossible. Through clear standards, proven reading instruction, accountability, and a refusal to accept failure as inevitable, it produced dramatic educational progress.
The question before us is simple:
**If Mississippi could change the trajectory of its children, why can 't Philadelphia?**
The F3 Forum will bring together parents, pastors, teachers, education experts, and community leaders for an honest conversation about where we are, what is working elsewhere, and what we can begin doing right here--in our homes, schools, churches, and neighborhoods.
I am honored to welcome an extraordinary group of speakers, including:
* **Corey DeAngelis** , nationally recognized education advocate
* **Dr. Lawrence Jones** , educator
* **Leah Ferretti** , founder of Mississippi Ready
* **Rev. Joshua C. Robertson** , senior pastor of The Rock Church
* **J. Allante McAuley** , Philadelphia activist
* **William Small** , Philadelphia entrepreneur
* A special presentation from the **former Associate Commissioner for Assessments at the National Center for Education Statistics, U.S. Department of Education**
* Dom Giordano, Host on WPHT 1210
* Chris Tremoglie, Reporter and Editor at Washington Examiner
* ...and more...

And yes--a delicious **Caribbean fusion lunch will be provided.**
We have intentionally kept the cost low because the people closest to the problem must be able to participate in building the solution.
If you **live in the Germantown area --or serve there as a pastor or teacher--there is no cost to attend.** However, you **must register** because seating is limited.
🎟️ **[RESERVE YOUR SEAT NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/569ce0f6-fd6b-4db0-97a7-4f5ec02c0bb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Then share this announcement with a parent, teacher, pastor, neighbor, or community leader who needs to be in the room.
The future of America will _not_ be determined in Washington, D.C.
**It will be determined in our homes, in our schools, and in our communities.**
On October 24, we begin in Germantown.
Let's build.
**Kathy Barnette**
Founder, Seed & Roots Initiatives

For the first time, I'm sharing the official announcement for our 2nd Annual Conference --this year, The F3 Forum: Faith, Family & the Future of Education in America--taking place Saturday, October 24, 2026, in the heart of Germantown, Philadelphia. 🎟️ Registration is now open! THE F3 FORUM: Faith • Family • the Future of Education in America Can Philadelphia Become America 's Next Mississippi Miracle? Saturday, October 24, 2026 9:00 a.m. -2:00 p.m. Doors open at 8:30 a.m. The Braid Mill 441 E. High Street Philadelphia, PA 19144 This isn't just another event. It is a community-wide conversation about literacy, opportunity, and student success --and what it will take to change the trajectory of Philadelphia's children. Last year, we gathered in Philadelphia for our inaugural Seed & Roots conference to focus on faith, family, and the future of work in America. This year, we are taking the conversation directly into the community--and focusing on one of the most urgent issues confronting our families: the education of our children. Mississippi accomplished what many believed was impossible. Through clear standards, proven reading instruction, accountability, and a refusal to accept failure as inevitable, it produced dramatic educational progress. The question before us is simple: If Mississippi could change the trajectory of its children, why can 't Philadelphia? The F3 Forum will bring together parents, pastors, teachers, education experts, and community leaders for an honest conversation about where we are, what is working elsewhere, and what we can begin doing right here--in our homes, schools, churches, and neighborhoods. I am honored to welcome an extraordinary group of speakers, including: Corey DeAngelis , nationally recognized education advocate Dr. Lawrence Jones , educator Leah Ferretti , founder of Mississippi Ready Rev. Joshua C. Robertson , senior pastor of The Rock Church J. Allante McAuley , Philadelphia activist William Small , Philadelphia entrepreneur A special presentation from the former Associate Commissioner for Assessments at the National Center for Education Statistics, U.S. Department of Education Dom Giordano, Host on WPHT 1210 Chris Tremoglie, Reporter and Editor at Washington Examiner ...and more... And yes--a delicious Caribbean fusion lunch will be provided. We have intentionally kept the cost low because the people closest to the problem must be able to participate in building the solution. If you live in the Germantown area --or serve there as a pastor or teacher--there is no cost to attend. However, you must register because seating is limited. 🎟️ Then share this announcement with a parent, teacher, pastor, neighbor, or community leader who needs to be in the room. The future of America will not be determined in Washington, D.C. It will be determined in our homes, in our schools, and in our communities. On October 24, we begin in Germantown. Let's build. Most everywhere I go, folks tell me the same thing: they're getting squeezed at the grocery store. North Carolina families have had enough, and I have too.
That's why as Governor, I worked with the USDA to increase funding for locally grown and produced food to distribute to local communities and schools. We have the best agriculture industry in the world right here in North Carolina, and it's great that our farmers get connected with schools to provide students with healthy, locally grown meals.
We also distributed $1.3 million in federal grants to help more public schools provide healthy school breakfasts for children in the classroom so they can start their day ready to learn and be successful. This initiative expanded access to school breakfasts for more than 51,000 students and followed $5 million in grants we dedicated to help underserved communities address food insecurity needs.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/8b97f861-8eaa-4fe3-992c-007cddb45f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
North Carolinians deserve access to affordable healthy food options. But right now, too many people are bearing the brunt of rising food costs.
I've heard from parents like Stephanie, who's struggling to balance rising grocery costs with the dietary and nutritional needs of her family. Her grocery bill has nearly doubled, and even as she works to keep up with rising child care and grocery costs, there's just too much month at the end of money.
And it's not just families feeling the pinch at checkout -- these rising costs are starting with our farmers. Right now, tariffs are driving up costs for the hardworking people who grow our food, and farmers have no choice but to pass those costs along to restaurants, grocery stores and North Carolinians. I've heard from farmers like Pender, whose costs have climbed because of federal policies that make it harder for him to afford the supplies he needs to grow crops and stay afloat.
Those costs get passed down the line, from the farm to the grocery store to your kitchen table. We've got to do more to support our farmers and put a stop to the chaotic tariffs that are making their jobs harder and your groceries more expensive. As Senator, I'll fight to roll back these erratic tariffs and take the burden off North Carolina's farmers.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/8b97f861-8eaa-4fe3-992c-007cddb45f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But tariffs are only part of the story. We also need to deal with the corporations that own our grocery stores and hold too much power over what we pay. When these companies merge, it reduces competition and prices go up for everyone. I'll work to hold them accountable by blocking anti-competitive mergers and strengthening antitrust enforcement across grocery retail and food processing. We have to block corporate mergers that reduce competition and raise prices.
And we know that these corporations are coming at North Carolina families from every angle, including using your own data against you. Some corporations are charging different people at different prices for the exact same groceries based on what they know about you. They're taking advantage of your family's grocery needs. That's not competition -- it's exploitation. I'll fight to ban algorithmic pricing in grocery sales and make it illegal for companies to raise the price of groceries for a specific consumer.
As your U.S. Senator, I'll fight to pass legislation that bans these practices and any other measures that unfairly raise prices for hardworking North Carolinians. And I'll work with anyone I can to get it done.
Families like Stephanie's and farmers like Pender should not have to keep absorbing the cost of a broken system. That's why I'm running for the U.S. Senate to make things cost less, starting with the price of food and groceries.
If you are ready to join me and fight for the people of North Carolina, please [chip in](https://substack.com/redirect/8b97f861-8eaa-4fe3-992c-007cddb45f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a few dollars or [volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/d467aaea-ee4a-4361-be2c-490bca0c09cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to knock doors. Let's get to work.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/8b97f861-8eaa-4fe3-992c-007cddb45f78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

I’ve called New Hampshire home for decades, and I can tell you plain and simple: Chris Pappas represents the best of the Granite State. He shows up, listens, and never backs down from a tough fight. This event will take place just one day before Chris’s final FEC end-of-quarter deadline, so we’re hoping for a huge attendance as a show of strength in the final days of his campaign. I’d be delighted if you’d join us. Thank you, Ken Burns New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?

In 2018, we backed candidates who were just getting started. Look at them now:
* **Abigail Spanberger:** A former U.S. postal inspector and CIA operations officer who spent nearly a decade working counterterrorism and national security cases before flipping a U.S. House seat in Virginia in 2018. Last November, she made history as Virginia's first woman governor.
* **Mikie Sherrill:** A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot who spent nearly a decade on active duty flying Sea King helicopter missions across Europe and the Middle East, including during the Iraq War, before flipping a U.S. House seat in New Jersey in a highly competitive 2018 race. In 2025, she was elected as the state's governor.
* **Elissa Slotkin:** A former CIA analyst who deployed on three tours to Iraq alongside the U.S. military before working national security roles at the Pentagon and White House. After flipping a U.S. House seat in Michigan in 2018, Elissa served three terms before winning a U.S. Senate seat in 2024.

This year, EMILYs List is again supporting a robust group of House candidates who spent years — and in some cases decades — serving in uniform before seeking elected office:
* **JoAnna Mendoza:** A retired Marine Corps drill instructor turned veterans' advocate who is running to flip Arizona's 6th Congressional District and beat Rep. Juan Ciscomani.
* **Jessica Killin:** An Army veteran and fourth-generation Colorado native who is taking on Rep. Jeff Crank in a bid to flip Colorado's 5th Congressional District.
* **Leela Gray:** A retired Army brigadier general and attorney who is challenging Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and making Florida's Republican-leaning 13th Congressional District competitive for the first time in years.
* **Nancy Lacore:** A retired three-star Navy admiral and former chief of Navy Reserve, removed from her post by MAGA extremist Pete Hegseth during a partisan Pentagon leadership shakeup, now running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District.
* **Rebecca Bennett:** A former Navy helicopter pilot and test pilot turned healthcare executive who won her crowded primary and is running to flip New Jersey's 7th Congressional District and beat Rep. Tom Kean Jr.
* **Cait Conley:** An Army special operations veteran and former White House counterterrorism director who is challenging Trump-endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler to flip New York's 17th Congressional District.
* **Kristina Knickerbocker:** An Air Force veteran and neuro-oncology nurse practitioner mounting a campaign against longtime incumbent Rep. Mike Turner in Ohio's 10th Congressional District.
* **Elaine Luria:** A retired 20-year Navy commander and former two-term congresswoman seeking a rematch against Rep. Jen Kiggans to reclaim her seat in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District.

Different branches. Different careers. Different parts of the country. But each of these women entered politics after already spending years in service to the country.
This election is about more than reclaiming power from the Trump administration — it's about changing who holds that power in the first place. That's the mission EMILYs List has always carried out: recruiting, supporting, and electing women who get real results and build a better future for all of us.

clean_body: EMILYs List is building the bench. | = Peter, In 2018, EMILYs List-endorsed women flipped 24 Republican-held seats in the U.S. House — singlehandedly delivering Democrats the majority. That class included women who came to politics after careers in the military, intelligence, and national security. Republicans were certain they'd hold on to their majority that year. They were wrong. And this year, we have the chance to do it again. = | = In 2018, we backed candidates who were just getting started. Look at them now: Abigail Spanberger: A former U.S. postal inspector and CIA operations officer who spent nearly a decade working counterterrorism and national security cases before flipping a U.S. House seat in Virginia in 2018. Last November, she made history as Virginia's first woman governor. Mikie Sherrill: A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot who spent nearly a decade on active duty flying Sea King helicopter missions across Europe and the Middle East, including during the Iraq War, before flipping a U.S. House seat in New Jersey in a highly competitive 2018 race. In 2025, she was elected as the state's governor. Elissa Slotkin: A former CIA analyst who deployed on three tours to Iraq alongside the U.S. military before working national security roles at the Pentagon and White House. After flipping a U.S. House seat in Michigan in 2018, Elissa served three terms before winning a U.S. Senate seat in 2024. This year, EMILYs List is again supporting a robust group of House candidates who spent years — and in some cases decades — serving in uniform before seeking elected office: JoAnna Mendoza: A retired Marine Corps drill instructor turned veterans' advocate who is running to flip Arizona's 6th Congressional District and beat Rep. Juan Ciscomani. Jessica Killin: An Army veteran and fourth-generation Colorado native who is taking on Rep. Jeff Crank in a bid to flip Colorado's 5th Congressional District. Leela Gray: A retired Army brigadier general and attorney who is challenging Rep. Anna Paulina Luna and making Florida's Republican-leaning 13th Congressional District competitive for the first time in years. Nancy Lacore: A retired three-star Navy admiral and former chief of Navy Reserve, removed from her post by MAGA extremist Pete Hegseth during a partisan Pentagon leadership shakeup, now running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District. Rebecca Bennett: A former Navy helicopter pilot and test pilot turned healthcare executive who won her crowded primary and is running to flip New Jersey's 7th Congressional District and beat Rep. Tom Kean Jr. Cait Conley: An Army special operations veteran and former White House counterterrorism director who is challenging Trump-endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler to flip New York's 17th Congressional District. Kristina Knickerbocker: An Air Force veteran and neuro-oncology nurse practitioner mounting a campaign against longtime incumbent Rep. Mike Turner in Ohio's 10th Congressional District. Elaine Luria: A retired 20-year Navy commander and former two-term congresswoman seeking a rematch against Rep. Jen Kiggans to reclaim her seat in Virginia's 2nd Congressional District. Different branches. Different careers. Different parts of the country. But each of these women entered politics after already spending years in service to the country. This election is about more than reclaiming power from the Trump administration — it's about changing who holds that power in the first place. Friends, I entered this race and hope to enter the Senate with one guiding principle: _What is best for the people of my state?_ Let me backtrack a bit and explain how we got to this point.
**_How we got here_**
Like many great ideas, this one started at home with my wife, LaVon.
Countless times over the last two years I have looked at what is happening in Washington and thought, _this is wrong_. This is not how our country is supposed to work. And it’s not a Republican thing or a Democrat thing; I believe _all of us_ care about decency and humanity. _No one_ is rooting for higher gas and grocery prices or people getting kicked off their health insurance.
The difference is that this time, LaVon responded, **“Maybe _you’re_ the somebody. Maybe _you_ need to do something.”**
**_How it’s going_**
It’s been a whirlwind since we launched this campaign. We went from zero to 60 very quickly thanks to a grassroots team that has shown incredible commitment.
The very same day I became the official Democratic Senate nominee, a new super PAC formed with the sole purpose of opposing me. They quickly went live with attack ads and have spent over $7 million so far.
But there was good news too. National election forecasters like The Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball upgraded our chances of winning, moving Kansas out of the “Safe Republican” category in their rankings. Real Clear Polling shifted us from “Likely R” to “Leans R.” Nate Silver shifted the race in our direction. Even Fox News took notice and moved this race in our direction.
**_What’s next?_**
I’m not going to pretend winning will be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are. The next 42 days will be busy, exhausting and expensive. If there’s one thing I’ve learned in my few months of running for office, it’s that running a campaign takes A LOT of resources (and winning will take even more).

clean_body: Why not me? Why not you? | | | = Friends, I entered this race and hope to enter the Senate with one guiding principle: What is best for the people of my state? Let me backtrack a bit and explain how we got to this point. How we got here Like many great ideas, this one started at home with my wife, LaVon. Countless times over the last two years I have looked at what is happening in Washington and thought, this is wrong. This is not how our country is supposed to work. And it’s not a Republican thing or a Democrat thing; I believe all of us care about decency and humanity. No one is rooting for higher gas and grocery prices or people getting kicked off their health insurance. The difference is that this time, LaVon responded, “Maybe you’re the somebody. Maybe you need to do something.” How it’s going It’s been a whirlwind since we launched this campaign. We went from zero to 60 very quickly thanks to a grassroots team that has shown incredible commitment. The very same day I became the official Democratic Senate nominee, a new super PAC formed with the sole purpose of opposing me. They quickly went live with attack ads and have spent over $7 million so far. But there was good news too. National election forecasters like The Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball upgraded our chances of winning, moving Kansas out of the “Safe Republican” category in their rankings. Real Clear Polling shifted us from “Likely R” to “Leans R.” Nate Silver shifted the race in our direction. Even Fox News took notice and moved this race in our direction. What’s next? name: Deb Haaland
subject: I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=1&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. I am the daughter of Pueblo women, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **And thanks to your support, I am the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=3&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
But no matter where I go and no matter what role I serve in, **I'm a proud Pueblo woman.** That's why I often wear my mocs or my ribbon skirt. These symbols remind me of how powerful traditional clothing is in sharing our heritage, and they remind me to honor the shoulders I stand on.

In a minute, I'm going to share some of the places I've rocked my ribbon skirt and mocs. [ _**But before I do, I have to ask:**_**_Will you please help fuel our fight to the general election by giving $5 to my campaign right now?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16526?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=4&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=5&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
| | On the day I was sworn in as Secretary of the Interior, I decided to wear my white moccasins and a handmade ribbon skirt adorned with butterflies, stars, and corn. No matter where I go, I am a proud Pueblo woman first — including at the Department of the Interior.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8175?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=6&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
| | On the first day of the White House Tribal Nations Summit in 2021, I wore my beaded moccasins in solidarity with our Indigenous people across the country. I am incredibly grateful that together, our administration made extraordinary accomplishments for Indian Country — enduring progress that would make our ancestors proud.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=7&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
| | From my ancestral homelands here in New Mexico to the halls of Congress — and as I filed my candidate petition to add my name to New Mexico's ballot for Governor — I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=8&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
Friend, history has shown us there’s nothing we can’t accomplish when we work together, which is why I’m counting on the support of people like you as we fight for a New Mexico that works for everyone.
This race is heating up, friend, and I need your help. **I am ready to fight for an education that gives every child the chance to dream big and reach their full potential here in New Mexico. Give families a raise by increasing the minimum wage and the child tax credit. Protect affordable healthcare for all New Mexicans who depend on it. And with less than six weeks to go until Election Day, we are one step closer to making this vision a reality.**

**_[Please, friend: Will you chip in $5 right now so we can build a strong campaign capable of winning this race and making history again?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16526?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=9&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1437-fr-nd&t=10&akid=12643%2E400544%2Eeww_Rs)
---
I am so grateful for your support. Thank you for being by my side.

Be fierce,
Deb

| Dear Peter,
You already know the contrast.
Mike Minogue would suspend the 24-cent state gas tax when prices top $4 a gallon and work to end the levy. Maura Healey's agenda points the other way: add a Miles Driven Tax in their unrealistic "Net Zero" plan.
The choice is simple. Minogue would pause a tax people already hate when prices rise. Healey's path treats driving itself as something to meter and bill.
Families paying more for gas, heat, and groceries do not need an odometer tax. They need a governor who will take the state's hand out of the tank.
But there is something you can do!
Post the contrast image above on your social media, call talk radio, write a letter to the editor! ( All the tools are below! )
Call three people and ask them to do the same. Send this to your friends and get them active!
We can win in November if we work together to hold Maura Healey accountable!
Sincerely,

| Amy Carnevale Chairwoman, Massachusetts Republican Party

Friend, It's Angie Craig. There’s a House race right next door to my district that I need you to know about, because it's one that Democrats can win. Jake Johnson has taught math in Rochester Public Schools for 20 years. He grew up in Stewartville, Minnesota, one of eleven kids, the son of a garbage collector and a meter reader, in a family that worked hard and still needed SNAP and Medicaid to get by. I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park, so I know exactly what Jake means when he says those programs were a lifeline. And he and his wife Molly are raising four boys — Cheryl and I have four sons, so I know what his grocery bill looks like, too. Jake is running against Brad Finstad, and I know Finstad's record better than most. As the top Democrat on the House Agriculture Committee, **I watched him lead the push to cut SNAP by $186 billion, all in the same bill that handed $1 trillion in tax breaks to the wealthiest 1%.** He's voted again and again to keep the tariffs that are squeezing southern Minnesota's farmers. And he hasn't held a single in-person town hall in four years. Jake has held 21, one in every county in the district. [**That's the choice in MN-01. clean_body: Join me in supporting the Democrat who's going to flip a house seat in Minnesota. | Friend, It's Angie Craig. There’s a House race right next door to my district that I need you to know about, because it's one that Democrats can win. Jake Johnson has taught math in Rochester Public Schools for 20 years. He grew up in Stewartville, Minnesota, one of eleven kids, the son of a garbage collector and a meter reader, in a family that worked hard and still needed SNAP and Medicaid to get by. I was raised by a single mom in a mobile home park, so I know exactly what Jake means when he says those programs were a lifeline. And he and his wife Molly are raising four boys — Cheryl and I have four sons, so I know what his grocery bill looks like, too. Jake is running against Brad Finstad, and I know Finstad's record better than most. As the top Democrat on the House Agriculture Committee, I watched him lead the push to cut SNAP by $186 billion, all in the same bill that handed $1 trillion in tax breaks to the wealthiest 1%. He's voted again and again to keep the tariffs that are squeezing southern Minnesota's farmers. And he hasn't held a single in-person town hall in four years. Jake has held 21, one in every county in the district. = Here's why I believe this seat is winnable. The DCCC put MN-01 on its Red to Blue list of the most flippable seats in the country. And just this month, Inside Elections moved this race toward Democrats. In 2018, Democrats came up 1,315 votes short in this district. Let's get it done in 2026. So folks, will you chip in $5 or more right now and help send a math teacher to Congress? If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = | = | = | = | = Thank you for standing with Jake. Let's go win this one. Two weeks ago, we settled against Meta (owner of Facebook and Instagram) for a guaranteed minimum of $451 million for our state.
It was part of the largest Big Tech settlement in American history.
Well, time for more big news.
We just reached a settlement worth nearly $600 million for North Carolina - _the largest environmental damage payment in state history._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/529b91da-e790-468c-8fe6-0ad723269944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is about the PFAS "forever chemicals" contamination in southeastern NC.
In short, a chemical plant outside of Fayetteville polluted the river for years with PFAS chemicals that don't break down. They last forever.
The plant was owned by DuPont and then Chemours. They knew the pollution was happening, they covered it up, and half a million people living downstream have suffered as a result.
We were hoping the EPA would take this seriously, but they failed. They could have really held these companies accountable, but instead they gave them a slap on the wrist.
So we stepped up, and now we've gotten at least 20x what the EPA got for our state.
_So Jeff, where 's the money going?_
Great question.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/98e25e05-983f-46ea-803c-f8c2de2a0cb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Announcement of PFAS settlement with local leaders in Cumberland County.
The biggest piece is going directly to the communities downstream that got hit the hardest. That was very important to us. Those communities have suffered for years and they deserve the biggest chunk of the payment.
The second piece goes to the state's PFAS cleanup fund. That will be about $55m.
The third piece is really important. Chemours has already been ordered to clean up their mess, and they have been forced to spend over $1 billion to do that.
BUT, there's a chance they could go broke. Given everything they now have to pay, bankruptcy for Chemours is a real risk.
If that happens, we need to make sure the cleanup continues, so for the third piece of the deal we made sure that if Chemours goes broke, DuPont will be on the hook to continue paying for the cleanup.
In other words, if the small company goes bust, the big company still has to pay.
For example, over 10,000 families in southeastern NC have had clean water systems put in their homes to ensure they have access to clean drinking water. We wanted to make sure everyone had that chance, no matter what happened to Chemours down the road.
Putting this settlement together was a massive effort - one of the biggest projects we've undertaken since I've been AG. The reason it was so big was because it directly involved a number of counties and towns. We wanted them to have the right to say yes or no to this deal, and after a lot of work, the commissions and councils all voted to approve - on a bipartisan basis. We cheered in our office when the last vote came through.
As for the EPA, look, I'm sure there are plenty of nice folks there, but they blew it on this one. They could have gotten really significant help for our state, but - for whatever reason - they essentially stood down.
But we stood up, because we actually live here. We look out for each other. And now, we're going to be in a much stronger position to ensure our neighbors have clean drinking water, _as they deserve._

That's the big news. More coming soon.

Best,
Jeff Jackson

clean_body: Largest environmental payment ever | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Largest environmental payment ever | | | Sep 22 | | | | | | | | | | | | Two weeks ago, we settled against Meta (owner of Facebook and Instagram) for a guaranteed minimum of $451 million for our state. It was part of the largest Big Tech settlement in American history. Well, time for more big news. We just reached a settlement worth nearly $600 million for North Carolina - the largest environmental damage payment in state history. | | ---|---|--- This is about the PFAS "forever chemicals" contamination in southeastern NC. In short, a chemical plant outside of Fayetteville polluted the river for years with PFAS chemicals that don't break down. They last forever. The plant was owned by DuPont and then Chemours. They knew the pollution was happening, they covered it up, and half a million people living downstream have suffered as a result. We were hoping the EPA would take this seriously, but they failed. They could have really held these companies accountable, but instead they gave them a slap on the wrist. So we stepped up, and now we've gotten at least 20x what the EPA got for our state. So Jeff, where 's the money going? Great question. | | ---|---|--- Announcement of PFAS settlement with local leaders in Cumberland County. The biggest piece is going directly to the communities downstream that got hit the hardest. That was very important to us. Those communities have suffered for years and they deserve the biggest chunk of the payment. The second piece goes to the state's PFAS cleanup fund. That will be about $55m. The third piece is really important. Chemours has already been ordered to clean up their mess, and they have been forced to spend over $1 billion to do that. BUT, there's a chance they could go broke. Given everything they now have to pay, bankruptcy for Chemours is a real risk. If that happens, we need to make sure the cleanup continues, so for the third piece of the deal we made sure that if Chemours goes broke, DuPont will be on the hook to continue paying for the cleanup. In other words, if the small company goes bust, the big company still has to pay. For example, over 10,000 families in southeastern NC have had clean water systems put in their homes to ensure they have access to clean drinking water. We wanted to make sure everyone had that chance, no matter what happened to Chemours down the road. Putting this settlement together was a massive effort - one of the biggest projects we've undertaken since I've been AG. The reason it was so big was because it directly involved a number of counties and towns. We wanted them to have the right to say yes or no to this deal, and after a lot of work, the commissions and councils all voted to approve - on a bipartisan basis. We cheered in our office when the last vote came through. As for the EPA, look, I'm sure there are plenty of nice folks there, but they blew it on this one. They could have gotten really significant help for our state, but - for whatever reason - they essentially stood down. But we stood up, because we actually live here. We look out for each other. And now, we're going to be in a much stronger position to ensure our neighbors have clean drinking water, as they deserve. That's the big news. More coming soon. Best, Jeff Jackson ? P.S. - On 9/11, I joined nearly 3,000 people at UNC's football stadium for the annual stair climb organized by UNC ROTC, where I was once a cadet. It was a record turnout, which was especially meaningful given that very few of the students who joined us were alive when the attacks occurred. Together, we climbed nearly 2,000 steps in memory of the firefighters, police officers, and other first responders who ran toward danger to help others. My thanks to the cadets who organized it, and to everyone who joined us to honor the fallen. | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Jeff Jackson Jeff Jackson for Attorney General, P.O. subject: Join Us Today: Who Pays for Power? | Climate Week NYC
body:
Across North Carolina and the country, data centers, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and other large energy users are driving new demand for electricity, water, transmission, power generation, and other infrastructure. | | | Greetings, 7 Directions Community, Today, 7 Directions of Service is bringing an important Indigenous-led conversation to **Climate Week NYC** , and we invite you to join us virtually. **WHO PAYS FOR POWER?**
**Indigenous Sovereignty, Data Centers & the New Energy Sacrifice Zones** 📅 **Tuesday, September 22, 2026**
⏰ **1:30–3:00 PM ET**
📍 **Live from The Monroe Room in New York City + Online** **The Monroe Room | 15 West 38th Street, New York, NY 10018** Joining us in person: Make sure your name is on the guest list; [RSVP here](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMc8Fed96CIUCvtTu0JxtYOjd3sfqf_AMlVgumes0AEDDKOvNILfBPycqXUMuAace_PeSB8gIeyrOZmYAOjNyNz6PwOVJi8ZYIO3wZHKbDBFL1iLDbCEjuaP-EmI8Hw43Ebc1j38c7cTKVMki5xU9VowAaXtK8XInR9hG3TPCzQU7yhDQOfzdCEYL9nhiEBiHDKrMndefcXlBkqs5ECeoWcRNgi5TLsMC9OiNOBGOQ8A4hT-e_EPzQHQ5FN37svP4rhul6w5gZE1GaPjx-8r99nrbyTGhFBWAEYxj0T7udaUtVSks3xhQrHZLou1ftwtO2z6ECyL1qenm2BjkSvLb4bA/4u9/Ga1rXFW9SR668UYHiGfiCQ/h0/h001.0lxYZ94vkfh29Z5AOvEiYq-WievC5uMiqop1DhQHA9s).
###
**Who benefits—and who pays?** For generations, Indigenous, rural, low-income, and frontline communities have been asked to carry a disproportionate share of the impacts from energy and industrial development. As we enter another period of massive infrastructure development, we cannot simply create a new generation of sacrifice zones. During today's roundtable, Indigenous leaders, organizers, advocates, and community voices will discuss:
* Who should pay for the energy infrastructure required by data centers?
* How could this new demand affect families and utility customers?
* What happens when development threatens water, sacred places, burial grounds, and culturally significant lands?
* What does meaningful Tribal consultation and consent look like?
* What can we learn from years of pipeline organizing?
* How can communities learn about projects earlier and organize sooner?
* How do we meet growing energy needs—including renewable energy—without creating new sacrifice zones?
* Could Rights of Nature provide communities with another way to protect land and water?

Most importantly, we will ask what communities can do **before** major decisions about their land, water, energy, and future have already been made.
### WATCH LIVE
You can watch and share the conversation through the 7 Directions of Service YouTube channel: [Watch 7 Directions of Service on YouTube](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMUBLAwgo3Db8YLyxpu0N8gK1iRX8K_viMiyMEax7zh2dcQ4mjkmeJ2ioXuGXW6WclpY4MZRKjYigtPeZTdT3667yczNg91j21jOMd-65QHnaZd0bCk0x7kN6zvrYO54CgLHCYwh_QPI2wXmZ1rs10Gf_7m9EW-KCCIY5nqv2dgmrlWbdSc7tKPOW_3OEG5OGlDhiyBrN0ZNT9A-q0Szhrz2SzycnOdiVKR0JZroxzrxyjjeTtY-ZdNkF8G0g9hxuxaGzgaJ1C3nf0T8UxRjPgweHADV9mIwoSQ3KB_Le-SFUQys1r60x7tLEu-YyjTs84kUrk5ft4nZxx8GkG0XeT-U/4u9/Ga1rXFW9SR668UYHiGfiCQ/h1/h001.8MVkq8c0t-OtgomofvPUI4olsqbTGFyY1IQw5eqmx4w) Please share the livestream with your family, friends, Tribal communities, environmental justice networks, and anyone concerned about the rapid expansion of data centers and energy infrastructure. **The energy transition has to change more than where our electricity comes from. It also has to change who has power in deciding how that electricity is produced.** And we should never accept a future where the same communities are continually expected to sacrifice their land, water, health, culture, and quality of life so that everyone else can have power. We hope you'll join us today. In solidarity, **Dr. Crystal Cavalier-Keck**
CEO/Executive Director
**7 Directions of Service** _Protecting land. Protecting water. Protecting sacred places. Building Indigenous power._

Meet Mark Harris:
**Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina.

Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt.

Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves.

clean_body: Don’t let them pass themselves off as moderates | Friend, There’s no such thing as a “moderate” who’s backed by Bernie Sanders, endorses Zohran Mamdani, and cheers on the defund the police circus. But that’s exactly the game being played by radical Democrats all around the country. Most notably, socialist candidate Rebecca Cooke is trying to slap a fresh coat of paint on her radical agenda. The strategy is familiar: soft language, carefully staged photos, and claims of “pragmatism”, while the actual record and endorsements tell a very different story. When someone is backed by Bernie Sanders, embraces figures like Zohran Mamdani, and aligns with the defund-the-police movement, voters deserve to know the truth. These are not moderates. They’re fighting for the same Radical Left agenda that has driven up crime, weakened law enforcement, opened our borders, and pushed extreme economic ideas that never work. I’m tired of the rebranding and the candidates who campaign as reasonable while governing as ideologues. And I’m tired of watching public safety and common sense take a back seat to radical socialist demands. This is why holding the House majority matters. Every seat that falls to candidates with records like these moves Congress further left and makes it harder to defend the policies that protect families, support police, and reject failed socialist experiments. | Thank you for standing with us, Rep. Mark Harris Meet Mark Harris: Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina. Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt. Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves. Mark and Beth have three adult children and eleven grandchildren, and call North Carolina home. Now, Mark is running for reelection because North Carolina deserves a fighter in Washington who will never stop standing up for faith, family, and freedom. The reporter put Mamdani on the spot, asking him to respond to Trump's White House Press Pool ban of CNN, Politico and MS Now, trying to create a moment of tension between the two men.
## [Trump absolutely let her have it! Watch here: ](https://substack.com/redirect/59d031f1-4b27-4841-9897-5bfbd2a2d6d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
# **Trump to address global crises in UN speech amid China meeting timing**
President Donald Trump **[will address the UN General Assembly Tuesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/69f29fe3-a254-408f-af1d-484f214979ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** covering Iran's nuclear program, the Gaza peace plan, and Western Hemisphere developments, with officials saying he'll argue his administration has confronted problems previous administrations let fester.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/69f29fe3-a254-408f-af1d-484f214979ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Iran is expected to dominate sideline diplomacy,** with Trump meeting Gulf Cooperation Council leaders afterward to discuss the war and Strait of Hormuz security, as a senior official said the U.S. continues its economic pressure campaign against Tehran.
* **Trump is also expected to renew calls for UN reform,** building on last year's criticism of the institution's effectiveness; officials say the administration has helped cut over $1 billion from the UN budget. Trump will then pivot quickly to China, meeting President Xi Jinping in Washington Thursday.

* * *
# **Trump launches "Trump TV" amid escalating media feud**
President Donald Trump**[launched the"Trump TV" streaming platform](https://substack.com/redirect/804c5147-192f-4085-8293-03790d09acae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Monday night after the five major networks -- CNN, NBC, ABC, CBS, and Fox News -- suspended their White House TV pool service in protest of the administration's ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico.
[| | | | | The White House
---
@WhiteHouse
IT'S LIVE. 📺🦅 TRUMP TV IS STREAMING NOW. 24/7, updated in real time, with top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place. Not every big moment has made it on your tv, now it can. 📲 youtube.com/@WhiteHouse
| 11:06 PM * Sep 21, 2026 * 60.5K Views240 Replies * 642 Reposts * 1.91K Likes

* **CNN, MS NOW, and Politico sued the administration Monday,** arguing the ban violates First Amendment protections; a hearing is set for Wednesday before a judge who previously ruled against a similar Trump-era press restriction.
* **The dispute escalated further** as major newspapers, including The New York Times and Washington Post, held back publishing presidential photos in solidarity, while the White House defended the access restrictions, saying credentialing rules have always favored allies rather than guaranteeing entry for every outlet.

* * *
# **Watchdog urges HHS to probe Planned Parenthood 's transgender treatments**
Do No Harm, a medical watchdog group, sent a letter to HHS asking for **[an investigation into Planned Parenthood](https://substack.com/redirect/50a5f751-a82a-4dc5-b5c1-dded7443dea8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** affiliates over allegations they may be using improper diagnosis codes to secure insurance reimbursement for cross-sex hormone treatments given to minors.
* **The group 's analysis, conducted with a data broker, identified roughly 800 patients age 22 and younger nationwide** who received 1,100-1,200 hormone prescriptions seemingly tied to gender dysphoria without corresponding proper billing codes for their office visits.
* **Do No Harm says such "miscoding" could help providers bypass insurance requirements** that treatments be "medically necessary," and points to a related HHS report alleging similar fraudulent billing practices across the broader transgender medical industry, while acknowledging its own investigation has limitations that warrant a fuller federal probe.

* * *
# **" Looksmaxxing" influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts**
Braden Peters, a popular Gen Z influencer known online as Clavicular, **[faces charges including rape](https://substack.com/redirect/db226a9e-d399-4c00-9082-afe367ba228a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and drugging someone for sexual intercourse in Massachusetts, tied to an alleged May 2025 incident; an arraignment is set for Oct. 14. His representative disputes the reporting's characterization.

* **Peters previously faced a civil lawsuit from another influencer,** Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, alleging he got her intoxicated as a minor and had non-consensual sex with her in 2025, then later injected her with an unapproved fat-dissolving treatment without consent during a livestream, allegedly suggesting methamphetamine was mixed in.
