clean_body: We are facing critical program gaps that could leave seats on the table and put a 2028 federal trifecta out of reach | | | | | TO: FROM: Emily Hogin, Vice President and General Counsel DATE: September 22, 2026 RE: Democrats Could Win Back Congress in 2026 Yet Still Lose the Midterms Peter, Democrats could win back Congress in 2026 yet still lose the midterms. Coming back from the brink of autocracy requires Democrats to win a federal governing trifecta in 2028 in order to hold the corrupt accountable, pass meaningful democratic reforms, and build a better future. If we fail to seize the opportunity to build back power at the state legislative level, we risk putting that federal trifecta out of reach before a single presidential candidate has declared. State legislatures elected this November will draw much of the 2028 House map and set the voting rules. State Legislators Will Draw Maps for the 2028 Congressional Election The redistricting wars won’t end in 2026. We need to win the right state legislative races this year to counteract extreme Republican gerrymandering and elect a trifecta in 2028 that could end gerrymandering forever. There are four states where Democrats have a path to a trifecta in 2026 that could lead to new Congressional maps and net seats for Democrats in 2028. State Legislators Will Set the Voting Rules for the 2028 Elections State legislators decide how easy or difficult it is to cast a ballot and have it counted. In a close election, these rules could make the difference. In 2024, Pennsylvania election officials rejected 10,598 absentee ballots statewide for technical errors. That is a substantial chunk of votes! And they didn’t all need to be rejected. The Democratic-controlled Pennsylvania House had passed a bill that would allow more votes to be counted notwithstanding technical errors, but that bill died in the Republican-controlled Senate. A new trifecta in Pennsylvania is within reach, but the program remains underfunded to date. Democrats must win the state legislatures that will decide whether there is a path back to federal power in 2028. Without state legislative power, there is no victory. If we only win Congress, we lose. The DLCC has helped recruit a strong group of candidates to seize the opportunity to build power in our state legislatures this year, but we are facing critical program gaps that could leave seats on the table and put a 2028 federal trifecta out of reach. ** Thank you, Emily Hogin Vice President and General Counsel Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee | | Prepared and paid for by DLCC Victory Fund, 1301 K St NW, Suite 300W, Washington, DC 20005. body:
Will you be one of the 8 people we need?

Peter,
We’re not relying on megadonors swooping in to save us with massive checks when we’re in trouble with our fundraising goals. No, that’s our MAGA opponent, Michael Whatley.
**We’re counting on people like you chipping in what you can, when you can – and right now, we need you.**
The GOP is going all in to defeat Roy and crush our grassroots movement. Super PACs are investing over $100 million to run baseless attack ads trying to turn voters against us, and we’re in dire need of more resources to fight back and run new ads of our own.
That’s why we have to reach our carefully calculated fundraising goals, including the one we’re facing today. That’s why we’re reaching out to top supporters like you, Peter.
**Here’s our plan: If just 8 people from your area chip in $5 to this email, we'll be on track meet our goal and surge ahead in this statistically tied race. We know not everyone can or will donate today, so we’re counting on YOU to be one of the 8.**
[**_Peter, will you represent your area with a $5 donation? If you care about flipping North Carolina and taking back the Senate for Democrats, we’re relying on your support right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1422&amount=5&t=8&akid=3746%2E124072%2EPdFAO3)

_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### David Shuster spent twenty years covering the Pentagon and Capitol Hill for MSNBC and Fox, which means when he tells you a cabinet secretary is finished, he is not guessing. He has watched this exact movie before. He was there in 2006.
##### Here is what he does in this piece that nobody on cable will do tonight: he goes and reads the House rule. Rule IX, privileged resolutions, two legislative days. That is why he can tell you exactly what the Speaker did last week and exactly why.

* * *
_**by David Shuster**_
Over the past two years, the Trump administration has delivered a string of horrifying spectacles. And there is every indication now that the public and political fallout will soon cost Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth his job.
Hegseth's controversies range from mishandling sensitive military information to draconian personnel changes at the Pentagon to trying to hide American military casualties and damage to U.S. bases across the Persian Gulf.
The controversies intersect with an extraordinary and recent development in the U.S. House: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie's effort to impeach Hegseth.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc073398-34ff-4e35-8023-dee41c488e4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Last week, before Republican speaker Mike Johnson suddenly put the House into an early recess, Massie introduced a privileged resolution seeking Hegseth's impeachment. Massie's eight articles accuse the defense secretary of, among other things, violating the War Powers Resolution, disregarding congressional restrictions on the Iran conflict, weakening civilian-harm protections, authorizing extrajudicial killings and engaging in other conduct that Massie characterizes as impeachable.
Under House Rule IX, a properly noticed privileged resolution receives precedence within two legislative days or 48 hours. However, the House doesn't have to wait 48 hours. The House could vote on the resolution immediately, which is usually what happens when the majority determines the resolution doesn't have majority support and can be eliminated.
* * *
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9d821cc9-b0bb-412c-85b2-1557f7ad3949?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc073398-34ff-4e35-8023-dee41c488e4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But a funny thing happened as Speaker Johnson tried to squelch the Hegseth impeachment and protect the Trump administration. Several Republican lawmakers indicated they would join Massie and all democrats in supporting the Hegseth impeachment. So, rather than allow a vote, Johnson put the House in recess for seven weeks until after the mid-term elections.

body:
We're already getting pummeled. It's about to get worse.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_2.s9rzqT&refcode=em20260922-2&t=1&akid=9069%2E582294%2Ed3onsm)
Please don't look away.
I just learned that crypto is dumping $30 million into defeating our campaign. Ohio is the only state they are targeting, and it’s with a historic amount in the final stretch of our race. **These attacks are imminent, and our response window is closing fast.[Please rush a split contribution between my campaign and Chris Pappas to help fend off these attacks.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_2.s9rzqT&refcode=em20260922-2&t=2&akid=9069%2E582294%2Ed3onsm)**
**[Rush $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_2.s9rzqT&amount=5&refcode=em20260922-2&t=3&akid=9069%2E582294%2Ed3onsm)**
There's a lot of moving pieces, but here's what I know right now:
Before this, the Republican establishment was already spending $14 million each week against us. That includes Jon Husted's super PAC, Elon Musk's contributions, Peter Thiel's dark money, and Donald Trump's multi-million dollar investment. _Every single week._
**With crypto jumping in, that weekly amount is skyrocketing.**
For reference, our campaign is currently spending about $2 million on TV ads each week.
Combined Republican spending is now at $238 million against me this cycle.
I'm never one to say the sky is falling or sound the alarm unnecessarily. But, unfortunately, this is not one of those times. **Crypto's new spending could bury us.**
They're doing it because Jon Husted is extremely vulnerable and the GOP has seen this tactic work before. In my 2024 race, when crypto started spending against me and we weren't able to respond, the polls started turning in Republicans' favor. _We lost that race._
A few weeks ago, Senate Republicans put out a call for outside groups like data centers and AI to bail Husted out with enormous cash infusions in the Ohio Senate race. **And, this is them answering the call.**
**We had no choice but to raise our fundraising goals so we could mount a response to these attacks from Big Tech. My team and I did the math and we need to raise $1 million so we can scale up our program _immediately._**
**[We have less than 24 hours to fend off their attacks and fundraise for our response. Right now is the single most important time for you to get involved. I cannot stress this enough – I need you to split $5 between my campaign and Chris Pappas right now. Please, while we still have time to launch a response:](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_2.s9rzqT&refcode=em20260922-2&t=4&akid=9069%2E582294%2Ed3onsm)**

Let's pull off an upset and prove Ohio isn't for sale.
In solidarity,
Sherrod

The Regime Open — September 22, 2026
Trump Threatened to 'Blow Away' Iran. Oil Fell 3.8% Anyway.
Markets had their best session in weeks on diplomatic hope, even as Trump's own UN remarks mixed a stark military threat with an openness to meet Iran's president directly.
|
---
Monday delivered the market's best session in weeks, built almost entirely on the diplomatic optimism this newsletter has tracked since the weekend — even as Trump's own words at the UN General Assembly's opening carried genuine menace alongside the hope. **Verified fact:** the S&P; 500 rose 1.06% to 7,731.78, the Nasdaq jumped 1.65% to 26,961.08, and the Dow gained 0.42% to 51,901.49, while crude fell a further 3.81% to $92.42 — now well below the $100 level breached Monday morning. As the General Assembly opened, Trump said “something very big” would happen soon on Iran, reportedly asking when the country would be “blown away, so they had better behave,” while separately saying he would “probably be open” to meeting Iranian President Pezeshkian.
| | Regime Signal 01 — Markets Chose to Hear the Softer Half of a Genuinely Mixed Message
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump described weighing three options for Iran — economic strangulation, military elimination, or a negotiated deal — in the same set of remarks where he raised the possibility of meeting Pezeshkian directly. **Our interpretation:** a 3.81% single-day drop in oil is a market decisively pricing the diplomatic option, not treating the military threat as the operative one. Whether that is well-founded conviction or wishful pricing depends entirely on which of Trump's three stated options actually gets chosen — and the rhetoric itself does not yet indicate which one is winning inside the administration.
| | Regime Signal 02 — The Physical Supply Story Kept Confirming the Diplomatic One
---|---
**Verified fact:** Monday's rally was also supported by confirmation that Saudi Arabia is restoring pipeline capacity and that crude exports have recovered from August lows. **Our interpretation:** this is the second consecutive session where a hard, physical data point (Hormuz throughput last week, pipeline restoration progress Monday) reinforced rather than contradicted the diplomatic narrative — a meaningfully more convincing pattern than the single-session, rhetoric-driven swings that characterized most of this month.
| | Regime Signal 03 — Two Summits, One Week, Still on Track
---|---
**Verified fact:** global equities strengthened broadly overnight into Monday, with technology and semiconductor names leading, as anticipation built for Thursday's Trump-Xi summit alongside the possible Trump-Pezeshkian UN encounter. **What remains unknown** is whether both diplomatic tracks can plausibly succeed in the same week, or whether markets are pricing an optimistic outcome on both that leaves limited room for disappointment on either.
| | Today’s Confirmation Point
---|---
Watch for any confirmed Trump-Pezeshkian meeting at the UN this week, and watch whether Trump's harder rhetoric — the “very big” warning and the three-option framing — produces any concrete follow-through that would contradict Monday's market optimism.

subject: He called me a lunatic

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3261%2E251025%2ED4-uvn ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3261%2E251025%2ED4-uvn ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, the
President of the United States recorded a video endorsing Mike Rogers, and
in it he called me a "lunatic" and an "America-hating communist."

[ A ]A screenshot of Trump's post about Mike Rogers and Abdul

I’m not surprised to hear more Mad Libs-style insults, because that’s
really all they have to work with. Not one word about your grocery bill.
Not one word about your healthcare premiums. Not one word about why your
utility bill keeps climbing.

Just my name, said with a combination of words pulled straight from a Fox
News headline.

Trump’s attacks don't faze me one bit. I love America, and I know our
campaign has the best platform to build a better future for all of her
people. Mike’s got nothing going for him.

But I'd be lying to you if I said this was only about words.

Trump is putting money behind his attacks. He's directing MAGA Inc., his
Super PAC, to spend more here in Michigan than in any other race in the
country:

[ A ]A screenshot showing where MAGA Inc., Trump's Super PAC, is spending
money. Michigan has the highest amount at over $18 million

Think about what that means. Of every Senate race in America, Michigan is
the one Trump wants to buy most.

He knows that this seat could decide control of the U.S. Senate, and that
if Democrats fall short here, Senate Republicans are practically
guaranteed to hold onto the majority.

We can’t let them blanket the airwaves with baseless attacks. That’s why I
set a goal of raising $5 million before our final end-of-quarter deadline
of the election cycle, and I’m counting on grassroots support to hit that
mark.

in $10 or any amount today to help us get ahead of Trump’s
spending here in Michigan before it’s too late:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260922-2-ak.lZo-dS&amount=10&refcode=em20260922-3256&t=1023&akid=3261%2E251025%2ED4-uvn ]Donate $10 ››

In solidarity,

Abdul

Because this isn't easy. It's an absolute dogfight, and you have to love the fight, really love it, to keep pushing when the odds are stacked against you.That's exactly what I've done. And I'm not backing down now.I've dedicated everything I have to flipping the US Senate seat in Minnesota, and there is no question in my mind that this is the right choice when I've seen first-hand what Peggy Flanagan and Tim Walz have done. name: Team Garrity
subject: Thousands of Pennsylvanians just stood up to Shapiro.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Garrity for PA * 4075 Linglestown Rd PMB 119 * Harrisburg, PA 17112-1020 * USA
body:
Superintendents, school boards, and thousands of Pennsylvanians told Shapiro to withdraw his health regulations.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Ozhg_822ZvG?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,

The public comment period on Josh Shapiro’s proposed health regulations just closed. Thousands of Pennsylvanians submitted comments — and the opposition was overwhelming.But I want to tell you about the comments that should worry Josh Shapiro the most. They didn’t come from politicians. They came from the superintendents and school boards who would actually have to carry out these regulations in your child’s school.**And they said no.** The superintendent of the tenth largest school district in Pennsylvania, wrote:_“Public health investigations should remain primarily the responsibility of agencies with the personnel, expertise, and legal authority to conduct them.”_ He warned that these regulations would force schools into an impossible position: “A policy that places school officials in the position of arranging confidential health-related conversations while potentially excluding parents could create long-term damage to the trust schools work hard to build with families and pose legal liability issues.”**The Pennsylvania School Boards Association** , representing more than 5,000 school directors and administrators statewide, agreed:_“The proposed regulation places schools in an untenable position between parents and public health authorities.”_ A superintendent in Bedford County got personal:_“As a parent myself, I would be extremely uncomfortable knowing that an outside government representative could meet privately with my child at school without my knowledge.”_ And she added something that a lot of us are thinking: “The time lost six years ago can never be regained, and I don’t want to see us make the same detrimental mistakes twice.”Two superintendents of two school districts in Northeast Pennsylvania put it as plainly as anyone:_“Our schools are educational institutions, not public health agencies.”_**That’s the bottom line.** These are career educators who care about their students and their communities. They’re not playing politics. They’re telling Harrisburg that these regulations would put children in rooms alone with government officials, cut parents out of the process, and turn schools into something they were never meant to be.Thousands of Pennsylvanians filed comments opposing these regulations. The voices were overwhelming. The question now is simple: will Josh Shapiro listen to the people he’s supposed to serve, or will he ignore them?

To put it plainly, we wouldn’t be able to do any of that without the support of grassroots donors. We’re doing the work to overcome the millions of dollars of shady PACs like Trump and Musk’s — and time is running out to organize and mobilize voters in these critical districts before Election Day. Thank you, Voto Latino

# Six Weeks Until the Election!
# Two Visions. One Choice.
---
|
---
| |
Last week, I stood on stage at the Bing Crosby Theater with Carmela Conroy for a debate hosted by _The Spokesman-Review_ and KSPS. It was a chance for voters to hear directly from both of us, and the differences could not have been clearer. We have fundamentally different ideas about the direction of the country: what it means to secure our border, strengthen our economy, stand up to China, protect American energy, and put the interests of Eastern Washington first. Ms Conroy wants higher taxes, more government control, men in women’s sports, “beheading” the DEpartment of Homeland Security and bringing in more illegal immigrats. This isn’t just a difference of opinion. It is a choice between two very different visions for America.
And that is why now is the time to act. If you believe America is worth fighting for, now is the time to get off the sidelines. Talk to your neighbors. Bring a friend to an event. Volunteer. Put up a sign. Make the phone calls. Knock on a door. Most importantly, make sure you and your fellow Republicans show up and vote. The future of Eastern Washington and the direction of our county will be shaped by those who choose to participate. I am in this fight, and I’m asking you to stand with me. Let’s get to work!
---
|
---
| |
# Join Us for WSU & Gonzaga Greats for Baumgartner- September 29th
---
|
---
| | Don't miss this special evening with two of Northwest’s most beloved sports legends, WSU football’s great Jack Thompson and Gonzaga basketball’s start Rob Sacre, as they join Congressman Michael Baumgartner on Tuesday September 29th! Enjoy an exclusive reception at the home of Subarna and Dave Nagra in Spokane, with VIP tickets at $500 and General Reception tickets at $250. Meet Jack and Rob and stand with Congressman Baumgartner as we keep fighting for Eastern Washington. RSVP today! Call or text Anitra at (253) 241-2420 or email her at anitra@votebaumgartner.com.

---](https://us.list-manage.com/17G8owMTTfV?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)

Team Baumgartner rolled into Sprague for the parade, and once again, Eastern Washington showed us how it’s done! The streets were lined with friendly faces and plenty of hometown spirit. Our team was out there meeting folks, handing out signs, waving, and making sure everyone knew that Team Baumgartner is on the ground and in the fight! Thank you to every volunteer who takes time out of their day to show up, represent our campaign, and bring that Eastern Washington energy to communities across the district.

|
---
| |
# Eastern Washington Fair Season
---
|
---
| | The Palouse Empire Fair has been a special event for our family for many years! It was great to be back at the fairgrounds this year with my parents and Maria (a huge fan of all the animals, and the amazing face paint!)
From Palouse to Columbia County to the Spokane County Fair, our local Republican teams have been right in the middle of it all over these past days: talking with neighbors, answering questions, and celebrating everything that makes this region special. A big thank you to every volunteer who staffed a booth. You are the heart of this campaign!

Team Baumgartner had a great time at the Deutschesfest Parade in Odessa! The streets were filled with colorful floats, German heritage, and plenty of friendly faces. Our volunteers were proud to be there, connecting with neighbors, and enjoying this fantastic annual tradition. It was another great day celebrating the people of Eastern Washington!

Cole’s no stranger to a congressional campaign (his name will be familiar!), and both of them represent the kind of young energy that keeps this effort strong across Eastern Washington.

A lot has happened since this mandate, and we've worked incredibly hard each and every day to deliver on the agenda we campaigned on that the American people so rightly deserve.

We cut through ALL the noise that the far Left propagated and intimidation tactics from Kamala Harris and her cronies.
Even after she raised $81 million in the first 24 hours after she officially announced her run for the presidency.

As we approach the elections this fall, we know a wave of far-left cash from their mega donors is just around the corner, and we need to do everything in our power to prepare to thwart these efforts.

That means when a good friend of mine personally calls in a favor, I don't hesitate to help him out.

If you're not familiar with Derrick Van Orden, I'll introduce you.Here's his story:

Derrick boasts the longest active-duty service in all of the United States Congress, serving over 26 years defending our freedoms, many of which were as part of the elite Navy SEALs.

Born and raised a Midwesterner, Derrick's toughness didn't just come from his time in active duty. He was raised by a single mother, whose father left when he was just a young boy.

For many, this would be enough to derail any childhood ambitions or sense of direction.

Not for Derrick.

He learned to be self-reliant from a very young age, and this attitude propelled him toward a successful military career for many years.
But the story doesn't end there...

It means more ads, more ground game, more voter contact, and more of the infrastructure that wins races in October. ]() That is genuinely good news. And we do not say that enough. Nationally, Democratic Senate candidates are outraising Republicans in seven GOP-held Senate seats. The same national liberal donor network that has been targeting this state all cycle is still writing checks because flipping a Senate seat in President Trump's home state would be the biggest symbolic victory the Left could claim in 2026. | | Peter, You know those political emails where you thoughtfully answer a survey or poll only to find you need to donate to submit? _Not this time._ No donation required -- just your honest opinion. Grassroots patriots like you are the heartbeat of the America-First movement, and we are taking the pulse as we race towards the 2026 midterms. Take two minutes and weigh in below.

clean_body: I think you should hear it| | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

Derrick boasts the longest active-duty service in all of the United States Congress, serving over 26 years defending our freedoms, many of which were as part of the elite Navy SEALs.

Born and raised a Midwesterner, Derrick's toughness didn't just come from his time in active duty. He was raised by a single mother, whose father left when he was just a young boy.

For many, this would be enough to derail any childhood ambitions or sense of direction.

Not for Derrick.

He learned to be self-reliant from a very young age, and this attitude propelled him toward a successful military career for many years.
But the story doesn't end there...

After his time in uniform, Derrick found another way to serve, but in a different capacity. In 2022, he was elected to Congress after defeating his Democratic challenger in a purple district and then successfully fended off the seat in 2024.Now, she's trying to take him down again!

The U.S. Constitution was made "only for a moral and religious people" and is "wholly inadequate to the government of any other." John Adams 1798
**They Thought It Was Math Help. Then the State Took Their Daughter.**
In December 2024, Joseph and Arlene Kutzko -- devout Catholics from Southborough, Massachusetts -- lost custody of their 15-year-old daughter, Sophie, to the Department of Children and Families. Nearly two years later, they remain almost entirely cut off from her under a restraining order, while DCF, they say, supports a gender transition they refused to authorize. Their near-term fear is a specific one: that the state will start their daughter on testosterone. "The most important thing is to bring her back to our family," Joseph Kutzko said recently. "But a shorter term goal is to prevent them from giving her testosterone."
How does a family arrive at this place? According to the Kutzkos -- and, strikingly, to the U.S. Department of Education's own summary of their complaint -- the sequence began at Algonquin Regional High School, where their daughter attended after-school sessions her parents understood to be extra help for a math class. Those sessions, the parents allege, were actually gender-transition counseling. School staff, they say, began using a male name and male pronouns for her at school without informing them. And when the Kutzkos declined, on grounds of Catholic teaching, to affirm their daughter as a boy, a school counselor reported the family to DCF. The state then did what the school had begun: it took over...

It does not prevent the administration from pursuing the policy for future elections, and the lawsuit will continue after November.** That is why I’m staying in this fight. Nearly 4 million Washingtonians voted using ballots they received by mail in 2024. That makes protecting our established system especially important. **[The Supreme Court gave us a reprieve for 2026. When I started my first business, I prayed it would be successful... **God answered.**
When I was deployed to Afghanistan, I prayed my family would be safe... **God answered.**
When I saw career politicians turn their backs on Americans to put their pet projects before the interest of the American people, I prayed for a better outcome...
I was surprised when **_God called on ME_** to run for office.
I'm Troy Downing. You might not recognize my name, but that's okay.
I'm a combat veteran. A God-fearing Christian. A husband & a proud dad.
**[I'm also the Republican running for re-election in Congress for Montana in the biggest race in the country.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkyMl9GRy1ESC4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMzE5NjgtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MjJfRkctREguMTEwMTE3X3QyMDMxOTY4LTI4OTkifQ/talWpPcDft9FiuuLu9GAiA)**

**__But I'm at my wits' end with two-faced politicians and DC bigwigs who say one thing to your face, only to turn around & stab hard-working folks like you & me in the back.__**
I'll always tell the truth. I'll always put America first. I'll always stand up for what's right.

Here is the problem I set out to fix. Right now, if a dishonest tax preparer commits fraud on your return without your knowledge, you can be stuck facing IRS penalties with no time limit. Innocent people have spent months cleaning up messes they never made. My office alone has handled more than 1,400 IRS-related constituent cases. I have seen this frustration firsthand. The cases are staggering. One preparer on Long Island pleaded guilty to a nearly $12 million fraud scheme. In the Bronx, another ran a decade-long, $145 million scheme filing tens of thousands of false returns. clean_body: Friends, I have some good news, and then a favor to ask. This week, the House unanimously passed my bill, the Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act. | Friends, I have some good news, and then a favor to ask. Last week, the House unanimously passed my bill that protects taxpayers from ghost preparers. | Here is the problem I set out to fix. Right now, if a dishonest tax preparer commits fraud on your return without your knowledge, you can be stuck facing IRS penalties with no time limit. Innocent people have spent months cleaning up messes they never made. My office alone has handled more than 1,400 IRS-related constituent cases. I have seen this frustration firsthand. The cases are staggering. One preparer on Long Island pleaded guilty to a nearly $12 million fraud scheme. In the Bronx, another ran a decade-long, $145 million scheme filing tens of thousands of false returns. | My bill makes it simple. The unlimited statute of limitations should only apply when the taxpayer actually intended to commit fraud, not when a crooked preparer acts alone. Responsibility belongs on the people who broke the law, not the innocent taxpayers they burned. | It passed the House with support from both parties. Now it heads to the Senate. Here is my favor. This is the kind of practical, get-it-done work I was sent to Washington to do. But I can only keep delivering results like this if I keep this seat, and the left is spending big to take it from me. | | | | | | Thank you for standing with me. Sincerely, Nicole | Nicole for New York, PO Box 60487, Staten Island, NY 10306

name: Team Pappas
subject: We want to be open with you about the situation:
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Chris Pappas for Senate

We want to be open with you about our recent fundraising numbers.

After Chris became the official Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in New
Hampshire, we saw a surge of grassroots support.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_4.ZnThJj&refcode=em20260922-4&t=1003&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Screenshot of an ActBlue map showing nationwide donations

We’re so grateful for everyone who stepped up.

But now our fundraising has started to slow down – and it’s happening at
the worst time. Take a look at our recent fundraising pace:

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_4.ZnThJj&refcode=em20260922-4&t=1004&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Screenshot of an ActBlue chart showing donations trending downward

John Sununu is leading this race by 2 points, and national Republicans are
already planning to spend over $50 million to buy this open Senate seat.

That’s why we’ve set an ambitious $1 million goal for our end-of-quarter
deadline. We know that’s a big number, but there’s good news: We’re
already 54.3% of the way there.

Now we just need to close the gap over the next 8 days, and that starts
today.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_4.ZnThJj&refcode=em20260922-4&t=1006&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Our records indicate you haven’t donated since we won the Democratic
primary. If we can count on your support, will you chip in $5 or any
amount that makes sense for you today to help us stay on track to close
that gap and put our campaign in the strongest position for the final
stretch to November?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260922_4.ZnThJj&amount=5&refcode=em20260922-4&t=1025&akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_ ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris Pappas for Senate

P.S. If you have donated recently by check or mail, our digital records
may not reflect that at this time, and we appreciate your support!

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9073%2E582294%2EHJyq6_

This is what happens when we refuse to let cynicism have the final word.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260922-1&t=1&akid=4046%2E587540%2EjWg7Uo)
I don’t think we’re screwed, Peter.
Most of you probably don’t know this, but I’m a pretty cynical person. Watching the chaos unfold around us every single day, it’s hard not to feel like everything’s on fire.
So I mean it when I say — **I have hope.**
Seriously. It took us decades to get here. Years of organizing, building, losing, and trying again to get to this moment. But right now, our momentum is undeniable. Progressive Democrats are winning across the country, and when they get to office, they’re putting working class priorities front and center, where they should’ve been all along.
In the last year alone:
* We helped elect our first member of Congress, **Christian Menefee** who is now sitting on the House Oversight Committee helping lead investigations into the Trump administration’s corruption.
* **Mayor Mamdani** has secured a $1.2B deal with the state to deliver universal childcare and won more than $34M in settlements from predatory landlords. We’re proud to have been early supporters in his primary campaign.
* Our youngest Georgia state legislator, **Akbar Ali** helped push through a 60 day gas tax suspension that saved Georgians nearly $200M at the pump.
* Dems have flipped 30+ state legislative seats from red to blue since Trump took office.

I’m not saying everything is fine. It’s not. There are dark moments, and there will be more of them. But we can’t allow despair to become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
The people hoarding power are actively counting on our exhaustion. They _need_ us to be convinced that meaningful change is impossible. But that couldn’t be further from the truth.
**It’s no longer a question of _if_ change is coming — it’s already on the way because we demanded it. The question now is how big it’s going to be. And it’s _you_ that helps determine that.**
When you support our candidates and our mission, you help us clear the path for the leaders we deserve, who will fight for a future we can actually feel hopeful about.
We’re proud of the momentum we’ve built so far, but **the only way we keep it up is to keep our foot on the gas from now all the way to November.** That’s why I need you to step up today, Peter.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to power our work and help us elect the next generation of bold young leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260922_1_hopecore.NLt6Jz&refcode=em20260922-4046&amount=5&t=2&akid=4046%2E587540%2EjWg7Uo)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/ik_2nOMR_VX?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

Angie Nixon won Florida's Democratic Senate primary. Here's why that matters more than you know.

---

| Friend, [I need to tell you something about what happened in Florida, and _**I need you to understand that this isn't about money.**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycksGO3CwMx5-G3BiBgWRyyOGTotz2O1Sj9oi84CRsE5ICmd2-fZWZ6Qv0-sf8_LPlH2_2DcMS4vQ_rtSlMtqU7bhsKXh0M8aJPN0p_S5ziJMFATUXLQew6Eq4k9VY-c47j9JV1MmmFVIYra_V3DXOX6_atNI441wrm3f0DjxBS06bGqrQnTzRAshWCa0vI4wS0HmDRnkwLdMCF0rlkmg_3pfgMBbMP8ctObq4ba2Wbi5lz0z9x2BgMGRyR6LLZ4iJ_FnBYIgpOwbD_f6LjwuP4WuL_BNTDHHiH2U-InHiO54ANRxltSv5cKxM9bRiWBjUZ1gcU_232wD8r_PrIW9HcsRUv8FqT8wjdbjuGKbIVP_o-Nroq-9COZcZI_8o9qlgn5bPv1ssFAtT_XhEnzDkECcGNa5l33IoYTux-plopnopBIM6nbOns1T1JR3EoKYvW4Jnqn86y6u93fj320XKRl9bW0BAY5qWm8ZUqfP7Z1iWkOuGaTGdsz92XP7tKu4d_AkAAP__PIbIiA) Angie Nixon won the Florida Democratic Senate primary. She raised a fraction of what her opponent had. She was outspent 16 to 1. And she won anyway, by 12 points. That should stop every Republican in their tracks. Because here's what that result tells me: For the first time in history, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has won a major-party nomination for statewide office. The DSA , the same movement that swept New York and is reshaping the Democrat Party from the inside, just planted their flag in Florida. _And they did it without the money._ Nixon's win caught many off guard. Now the party has a DSA-aligned Senate candidate on the ballot in one of the most watched races in the country. This is the moment I've been warning about all summer. The conventional wisdom in Washington has always been that socialism can't win in Florida. That the money would win. That the establishment would hold. [_**Every one of those assumptions just got proven wrong.**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycksGO3CwMx5-G3BiBgWRyyOGTotz2O1Sj9oi84CRsE5ICmd2-fZWZ6Qv0-sf8_LPlH2_2DcMS4vQ_rtSlMtqU7bhsKXh0M8aJPN0p_S5ziJMFATUXLQew6Eq4k9VY-c47j9JV1MmmFVIYra_V3DXOX6_atNI441wrm3f0DjxBS06bGqrQnTzRAshWCa0vI4wS0HmDRnkwLdMCF0rlkmg_3pfgMBbMP8ctObq4ba2Wbi5lz0z9x2BgMGRyR6LLZ4iJ_FnBYIgpOwbD_f6LjwuP4WuL_BNTDHHiH2U-InHiO54ANRxltSv5cKxM9bRiWBjUZ1gcU_232wD8r_PrIW9HcsRUv8FqT8wjdbjuGKbIVP_o-Nroq-9COZcZI_8o9qlgn5bPv1ssFAtT_XhEnzDkECcGNa5l33IoYTux-plopnopBIM6nbOns1T1JR3EoKYvW4Jnqn86y6u93fj320XKRl9bW0BAY5qWm8ZUqfP7Z1iWkOuGaTGdsz92XP7tKu4d_AkAAP__PIbIiA) Friend, I am not writing to you today to ask for a dollar. I am writing because what happened in Florida is a signal, and as Senate majority leader, I cannot ignore it. And neither can you. [The socialist left has figured out something important. **They don't need to outspend us. They need to out-organize us.** They need their voters verified, mobilized, and ready before we even realize what's happening.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycksGO3CwMx5-G3BiBgWRyyOGTotz2O1Sj9oi84CRsE5ICmd2-fZWZ6Qv0-sf8_LPlH2_2DcMS4vQ_rtSlMtqU7bhsKXh0M8aJPN0p_S5ziJMFATUXLQew6Eq4k9VY-c47j9JV1MmmFVIYra_V3DXOX6_atNI441wrm3f0DjxBS06bGqrQnTzRAshWCa0vI4wS0HmDRnkwLdMCF0rlkmg_3pfgMBbMP8ctObq4ba2Wbi5lz0z9x2BgMGRyR6LLZ4iJ_FnBYIgpOwbD_f6LjwuP4WuL_BNTDHHiH2U-InHiO54ANRxltSv5cKxM9bRiWBjUZ1gcU_232wD8r_PrIW9HcsRUv8FqT8wjdbjuGKbIVP_o-Nroq-9COZcZI_8o9qlgn5bPv1ssFAtT_XhEnzDkECcGNa5l33IoYTux-plopnopBIM6nbOns1T1JR3EoKYvW4Jnqn86y6u93fj320XKRl9bW0BAY5qWm8ZUqfP7Z1iWkOuGaTGdsz92XP7tKu4d_AkAAP__PIbIiA) That is exactly what they are doing right now in Florida. And in Michigan. And in Maine. And in North Carolina. _The money doesn't matter if we don't show up._ That's why I am personally asking you to verify your 2026 Voter Profile right now. Not because it costs anything. Not because we need your donation. Because the only way Ashley Moody holds that seat in November is if every verified Republican in this country is counted, ready, and impossible to ignore. Angie Nixon proved that this fight is about people, not money. [_**So is this my request.**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycksGO3CwMx5-G3BiBgWRyyOGTotz2O1Sj9oi84CRsE5ICmd2-fZWZ6Qv0-sf8_LPlH2_2DcMS4vQ_rtSlMtqU7bhsKXh0M8aJPN0p_S5ziJMFATUXLQew6Eq4k9VY-c47j9JV1MmmFVIYra_V3DXOX6_atNI441wrm3f0DjxBS06bGqrQnTzRAshWCa0vI4wS0HmDRnkwLdMCF0rlkmg_3pfgMBbMP8ctObq4ba2Wbi5lz0z9x2BgMGRyR6LLZ4iJ_FnBYIgpOwbD_f6LjwuP4WuL_BNTDHHiH2U-InHiO54ANRxltSv5cKxM9bRiWBjUZ1gcU_232wD8r_PrIW9HcsRUv8FqT8wjdbjuGKbIVP_o-Nroq-9COZcZI_8o9qlgn5bPv1ssFAtT_XhEnzDkECcGNa5l33IoYTux-plopnopBIM6nbOns1T1JR3EoKYvW4Jnqn86y6u93fj320XKRl9bW0BAY5qWm8ZUqfP7Z1iWkOuGaTGdsz92XP7tKu4d_AkAAP__PIbIiA) | [**VERIFY YOUR PROFILE NOW >>**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycksGO3CwMx5-G3BiBgWRyyOGTotz2O1Sj9oi84CRsE5ICmd2-fZWZ6Qv0-sf8_LPlH2_2DcMS4vQ_rtSlMtqU7bhsKXh0M8aJPN0p_S5ziJMFATUXLQew6Eq4k9VY-c47j9JV1MmmFVIYra_V3DXOX6_atNI441wrm3f0DjxBS06bGqrQnTzRAshWCa0vI4wS0HmDRnkwLdMCF0rlkmg_3pfgMBbMP8ctObq4ba2Wbi5lz0z9x2BgMGRyR6LLZ4iJ_FnBYIgpOwbD_f6LjwuP4WuL_BNTDHHiH2U-InHiO54ANRxltSv5cKxM9bRiWBjUZ1gcU_232wD8r_PrIW9HcsRUv8FqT8wjdbjuGKbIVP_o-Nroq-9COZcZI_8o9qlgn5bPv1ssFAtT_XhEnzDkECcGNa5l33IoYTux-plopnopBIM6nbOns1T1JR3EoKYvW4Jnqn86y6u93fj320XKRl9bW0BAY5qWm8ZUqfP7Z1iWkOuGaTGdsz92XP7tKu4d_AkAAP__PIbIiA)

Donald Trump’s ICE is an utter disgrace to our country. Witnessing their unnecessary violence and cruelty over the past year and a half has been simultaneously heartbreaking and enraging. In the San Diego area alone, nearly 18,000 people have been arrested by ICE since Trump took office — including at least 769 children. Treating our neighborhoods like war zones, wearing riot gear and using flash bangs and smoke grenades, rounding people up with mass arrests — NONE of that was necessary to enforce immigration law. In the middle of the worst Cyclosporiasis outbreak on record (with cases up 15-fold compared to last year), a beef recall after it was imported from Argentina and sold to Americans without being inspected at all, and near-constant recalls on lettuce, blueberries, eggs, cheese, mangoes, and more – Donald Trump thinks we should eliminate food inspection regulations entirely.

_Less oversight and no food safety checkpoints are exactly the opposite of what we need right now._

The three main agencies responsible for food safety – the FDA, USDA, and CDC – have already undergone massive federal funding cuts thanks to Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and RFK Jr.

→ The FDA has lost 20% of its workforce, the CDC has lost 25%, and the USDA has lost 27%.

→ The national advisory committee that used to advise our federal agencies on how to prevent food contamination has been completely disbanded.

→ The CDC used to have 11 scientists tracking food parasites; now it has only three.

_Our federal agencies meant to protect public health are already operating with a skeleton crew, and now Trump wants to gut what’s left._

As a doctor, I want to be direct with you: food safety regulations are more than just a bunch of red tape and headaches for producers. They’re why you can go to a grocery store and trust that what you put in your body won’t make you sick. They’re why massive Cyclospora outbreaks like the one from this summer are typically rare and preventable.

We’ve already seen the impact of these federal budget cuts on Americans as thousands more people have gotten sick compared to previous years. Eliminating these programs will cost lives, period.

**This is what happens when you put people in charge of our government and public health who don’t believe in science and who don’t listen to the experts.**

name: Jim Schultz
subject: It's time to build
body:
The AI revolution will proceed with or without us. Minnesota can't afford to say no.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/ba698f6d162c/the-briefing-from-mpbc-13062877?e=baf210d431)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
Six years ago, Marc Andreessen published an essay with a single challenge: “[**It's Time to Build**](https://us.list-manage.com/sBCYFhX5366?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83).” His argument — that America had grown better at producing reasons not to build than at building what its people needed — was right then. It is more urgent now.
AI has handed Minnesota a once-in-a-generation opportunity. But this revolution runs on physical infrastructure: power plants, transmission lines, data centers. The Upper Midwest is well positioned. In Pine Island alone, a proposed data center would deliver $20 million in developer-funded infrastructure and a $25 million fund for local schools.Something has shifted in Minnesota's politics — and it isn't the facts.
In 2024 and 2025, state Sen. Grant Hauschild championed legislation expanding Minnesota's data-center tax exemption, calling it “a net benefit.” Now he's running ads accusing his opponent of failing to “crack down” on data centers. That is not a profile in courage. It is a profile in polling.
While politicians like Hauschild cower, China is preparing a reported $300 billion AI-infrastructure build-out. Beijing understands that delaying American infrastructure advances Chinese interests.
**The AI revolution will proceed whether Minnesota participates or not. If we say no, the investment, the jobs, and the tax revenue go elsewhere.**
That is the argument I made in the _Star Tribune_ this week— and one worth considering.
[**Read “Don’t let data center angst derail Minnesota’s moment to build” here**](https://us.list-manage.com/115gqj9vWHt?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83)**.**
Working with you,
**Jim Schultz** President & CEOMinnesota Private Business Council
**P.S.** For $100 a year, you stop watching from the sidelines. [**Main Street Members of the Minnesota Private Business Council**](https://us.list-manage.com/U8NaDaMs_uC?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83) get real-time alerts on legislation, insider polling on Minnesota's political landscape, and principled advocacy showing up in St. Paul when you can't. That's less than $10 a month to be part of the organized private-sector counterweight this state desperately needs — at the exact moment it needs it most. [**Join MPBC here**](https://us.list-manage.com/gYwOfpbZ2u2?e=baf210d431&c2id=93c61d534406ea5269257c101c1d1f83)**.**

Friend,

Back in 2008, Barack Obama promised the American people he would _" fundamentally change America."_ He meant every word. Look at what has happened to our election laws since that promise.

**Consider what states across the country have done in the years since that promise.**
* Voter ID requirements have been weakened or eliminated in states that once required them.
* Ballot harvesting, once illegal almost everywhere, is now permitted in a growing number of states.
* Deadlines for counting votes have stretched so long that "election night" barely means anything anymore.

This erosion took nearly twenty years to unfold, but the damage it has done to our elections has been enormous.

Landmark Legal Foundation has been in this fight for decades, defending the Constitution in courtrooms across the country long before election integrity became a headline issue.

**And Landmark Legal Foundation continues to fight Obama 's terrible changes, case by case, court by court. **

That's why I'm asking every one of our supporters to help me raise $750,000 this year to keep this work moving, and I'm asking you to be part of it right now.

Please donate $10, $35, $250, or whatever amount you're able to give today.

[Support Landmark Legal Foundation](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=3d4d613ccff14e2d9a3cb054649319d9&_e=pGYM9gAhhW-ciNhStQIyDVH4T_D_lypCbfh7NmXcIchKTTKr1fH_VrZi22MKHGaocVgWGkH1NiBpGQeUS_EZkB6Nu83rk0f5fY_-Vau05qeCQ5xExwA3wcAS0NZ5B6p1pVkyfNfzjhgItnN6WlZ3AyCmqIm5HnQURLATwRRz49JcEPHICcGNKHGhhlcSICZIXcQ2YH8g939YrQthLHNketRalcMNleREB81-XdZpLBjfgmSxZDwhJW1C1667XgG_5xHKqaIh2X3z0t1CjUAnTZ7wlmzBkB3-S4Wn6c-9H0l-ncuY7UJXJgHkpYhZh4KKxNVWgOeBvemrcnEirbilPHGEgk_YFASC5M_Kl8BIFLKLsSll6iAIMdDk5nmBHAHVXb4kN7ctV5V-WocwTOMfk3FXwPkiGNNqKsCl9PuwmDJ-2mxIEumo3Ixl184zeEntffDnXA4nM1vHv-_yajk_P5w2Tg-l1NieUtXlommYZgh-lZ2sgwNrEzyJxhbQ-yZf6DW2YPPf2T__wPWatBEr10JiPcVI7Mk0dQi37iiNq935NyxlubNhpz2M1F4dgqs9gPEYKxkeuXB3r7ba_oaHqi7-JvF_azNwymTIKY2xrEEcEu8VGQDV7lOoEOLHPzuKAjQb3GsCZ4bkx-YyKcCoiQD58jXJs7Seeb3TXlEySuI%3D)

Here's what makes Landmark's approach different from most conservative organizations working on election integrity today.

**Defending Election Integrity**
In _Brnovich v. Democratic National Committee_ , Landmark helped win a critical Supreme Court victory defending an Arizona law that placed commonsense restrictions on ballot harvesting.

Arizona's legislature had passed the law to protect the chain of custody for mailed ballots, and opponents sued to strike it down.

**Landmark filed a brief defending Arizona 's authority to secure its own elections, and the Supreme Court agreed, upholding the law and confirming that states have wide latitude to protect against fraud. **

That ruling now stands as precedent for every state considering similar election security laws.

clean_body: Friend, Back in 2008, Barack Obama promised the American people he would " fundamentally change America." He meant every word. Look at what has happened to our election laws since that promise. Consider what states across the country have done in the years since that promise. Voter ID requirements have been weakened or eliminated in states that once required them. Ballot harvesting, once illegal almost everywhere, is now permitted in a growing number of states. Deadlines for counting votes have stretched so long that "election night" barely means anything anymore. This erosion took nearly twenty years to unfold, but the damage it has done to our elections has been enormous. Landmark Legal Foundation has been in this fight for decades, defending the Constitution in courtrooms across the country long before election integrity became a headline issue. And Landmark Legal Foundation continues to fight Obama 's terrible changes, case by case, court by court. That's why I'm asking every one of our supporters to help me raise $750,000 this year to keep this work moving, and I'm asking you to be part of it right now. Please donate $10, $35, $250, or whatever amount you're able to give today. Here's what makes Landmark's approach different from most conservative organizations working on election integrity today. Defending Election Integrity In Brnovich v. Democratic National Committee , Landmark helped win a critical Supreme Court victory defending an Arizona law that placed commonsense restrictions on ballot harvesting. Arizona's legislature had passed the law to protect the chain of custody for mailed ballots, and opponents sued to strike it down. Landmark filed a brief defending Arizona 's authority to secure its own elections, and the Supreme Court agreed, upholding the law and confirming that states have wide latitude to protect against fraud. That ruling now stands as precedent for every state considering similar election security laws. Fighting Lawfare in the Courts When the Colorado Supreme Court tried to strike Donald Trump from the 2024 ballot by stretching a 14th Amendment provision written for insurrectionists, Landmark fought back at the U.S. Supreme Court. The justices ruled 9-0 that Colorado had no authority to make that call, protecting every voter 's right to choose their own president. Landmark took on a similar fight when Special Counsel Jack Smith brought charges against President Trump. Our team argued that Smith's appointment violated the Constitution because the Senate never confirmed him to that office. Judge Aileen Cannon agreed, and the charges were dismissed entirely. Both cases protect the same principle. Voters decide who leads this country, and no court or unconfirmed official gets to override that choice.** Landmark needs your help today. Please select an amount below to help us reach our $750,000 goal this year. Thank you for standing with us, and for taking the time to read this whole email. Richard "Pete" Hutchison President & General Counsel Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

name: Dave Beckwith for Congress
subject: I've noticed a pattern in what Suhas says vs. what he does in Congress...
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
And it contradicts the promises he campaigned on.
| | | | Hi Friend,
Suhas Subramanyam has built this whole campaign on saying the right thing. But if we look at what he's done in Congress, one pattern shows up again and again: **every time his party's interests and VA-10's interests pulled in different directions, he chose his party.**
_I believe our district deserves a congressman who keeps his promises, especially the ones his whole campaign is built on._
**If you agree, I'd love if you could chip in to support my campaign.**
---
[CONTRIBUTE TO THE CAMPAIGN](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
Suhas said he would protect our democracy from extremists... **Then he voted against a House resolution condemning the DSA and openly accepted them as part of the Democratic party**
Suhas said he would fight corruption and stop members of Congress from trading stocks... **Then he voted NO on the Stop Insider Trading Act, while his campaign continued taking money through a donation platform that's been under federal investigation since 2023 for knowingly enabling fraud.**
Suhas said he would help keep the federal government open to avoid shutdowns that impact federal government employees who make up so much of this district... **Then he voted seven times to shut it down or keep it shut, and thousands of his own constituents got furloughed without a paycheck.**
Suhas said he would combat political gerrymandering... **Then actively campaigned for the very referendum that gerrymandered Virginia further, and when that got struck down, he backed the plan to pack our own Virginia Supreme Court.**
Suhas said he personally warned Barbara Comstock about the dangers of data centers ten years ago. _Ten years..._ **By his own account, he saw this coming, and he did nothing.**
This is what choosing party over people looks like in practice, and we have too many career politicians in Washington now doing the same thing.
**That's why, at the core of my campaign, I'm running to represent the people of this district above everything else.**
[SUPPORT THE CAMPAIGN THAT PUTS PEOPLE FIRST](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
| | | Elected officials only have their job because the people trusted them with their vote. That's something I take very seriously, and I'll work every single day to live up to that promise in Congress.
God bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

Membership helps sustain the party and gives more people a way to take part in it. | | | Peter, Last week, we sent you a note about what it actually means to be a dues-paying member of the PA Working Families Party: how dues members can participate, what comes with membership, and the different ways people choose to plug in. But there’s another part of the Membership Drive we want to talk about: **why growing our dues-paying membership matters so much right now.** This has already been a big year for the PA WFP. This spring, we were deeply involved in races across Pennsylvania, organizing alongside partners, knocking doors, raising money, and helping endorsed candidates with fundraising, communications, field and political support, and the campaign infrastructure they needed. Now, we’re heading toward November and continuing to support candidates across the state. And once this election is over, the next cycle won’t be far behind. In 2027, Philadelphia heads into another major municipal election year, with City Council seats back on the ballot. That might sound far away. In campaign time, it really isn’t. Strong campaigns take time to build. Candidates need to be identified and supported, relationships need time to grow, communities need to be organized, and fundraising and campaign infrastructure need to be in place well before Election Day. That’s a big part of why having a strong base of members matters. [**Dues-paying members contribute a recurring donation of $10 or more a month, or $120 a year. How many people can say they've put everything on the line and have been within striking distance of making history by flipping Minnesota - a Democrat stronghold - to the Republican column?Not many. Because this isn't easy. It's an absolute dogfight, and you have to love the fight, really love it, to keep pushing when the odds are stacked against you.That's exactly what I've done. And I'm not backing down now.I've dedicated everything I have to flipping the US Senate seat in Minnesota, and there is no question in my mind that this is the right choice when I've seen first-hand what Peggy Flanagan and Tim Walz have done. ### Where was the catastrophe?
For six months a question has hung over this crisis: yes, fuel is up, life is tighter, but... **where is the catastrophe?**
Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz was the conduit for roughly a fifth of the world's oil. In August, flows through it averaged just 7.6 million barrels a day, according to the International Energy Agency. Before the war, over 20 million barrels crossed the Strait per day--a drop of roughly **63%**. Put differently, **nearly two out of every three barrels that normally crossed Hormuz are no longer crossing it**. Cumulative export losses through the strait are approaching 2.8 billion barrels. Back in April, the heads of the IMF, World Bank and World Food Programme said the war had already triggered one of the largest disruptions to global energy markets in modern history.
And yet, the gas lines of the 1970s never came. The lights stayed on, the shelves stayed full, the gas stations stayed available (though expensive), and the trucks kept moving. Plenty of smart people have looked at that and concluded the system must be tougher than the pessimists believed.
The observation is right. But the conclusion skips the question that matters most: **what did the global energy system use to absorb the blow, and how much of it is left?**

### Savings are not income
Picture a household that loses a paycheck. It gets by on savings, and if you only watched what was on the table for dinner, you might not notice anything had changed. That doesn't mean that paychecks stopped mattering.
A hospital that loses grid power runs on generators, and the patients on ventilators keep breathing. That doesn't mean the electrical grid is irrelevant.
The world has kept global supply chains functioning in large party by spending down savings. The US has drawn down our Strategic Petroleum Reserve to historic lows, and we're not alone. Reasonable people should be paying attention to how long that can continue.
There is another useful distinction here, one of my favorite concepts in systems analysis: **stocks** versus**flows**.
A stock is an inventory. A flow is movement between inventories.
A reservoir -- a "stock" -- can keep water coming out of the faucet for awhile after the river feeding it weakens. (Both the faucet and the river are "flows.")
If you watch only the faucet, everything looks fine. If you watch the reservoir falling, **you understand how long "fine" can last.** Oil production and imports are flows. Inventories are stocks.
For six months, falling stocks have helped conceal a badly damaged flow.
I have spent about twenty years working in sustainable farming, community land trusts, ecological infrastructure, and cooperative governance across five continents. The first thing that work teaches you is that **a system 's health is measured by what it is standing on,** not merely by whether it is running today.
Here is what the world has been standing on since February.
**It started with luck.** Oil markets entered this crisis in surplus. By the second half of last year, supply was running more than two million barrels a day ahead of demand, and the excess was filling storage tanks, most of all in China. Nobody planned that cushion for this war. It was simply there when the war arrived.
**Then came deliberate measures.** IEA member countries released more than 300 million barrels from emergency reserves. Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates shoved as much crude as they could through pipelines and ports that bypass Hormuz, offsetting more than 500 million barrels of the loss. Producers outside the Gulf pumped harder. _And the world simply used less._ Economists call that last part _demand destruction_. It is a tidy phrase for factories slowing, trips not taken, businesses cutting production, governments rationing fuel, and people who simply cannot afford what they used to buy.
The bypass story alone shows how hard the system adapted. Exports from Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal and the UAE's Fujairah port climbed from 4.1 million barrels a day in February to 7.8 million in June--**a 90% increase in four months.**
**The backup routes nearly doubled their workload.** Then Houthi attacks and other Red Sea disruptions knocked that flow back to 5.5 million barrels a day by August--a loss of nearly **30 percent from the June peak** -- _before_ the Saudi East-West Pipeline itself was hit on September 10th.
Even after all of that adaptation, the world has been pulling oil out of storage at a record 2.8 million barrels a day. Observed inventories now stand 507 million barrels **below** where they were when the war began. August alone drew down another 95 million barrels--almost one-fifth of the entire six-month inventory loss in a single month--showing that the _rate_ of drawdown is still increasing. That's disconcerting, to say the least.
The IEA's September 18 commentary contains a sentence everyone should read twice: "**if Gulf supplies stay constrained while commercial stocks keep falling, higher prices and further cuts in demand may be needed to balance the market. "**
Translated out of economist: if more supply cannot get through, and there is less stored oil available to cover the gap, the thing that eventually has to give is consumption. Prices will rise until enough people, businesses and countries stop buying.
So the honest description of the last six months is not that the shock was avoided.
**The shock was financed.**
We paid for it out of stored oil, emergency reserves, spare infrastructure, increased production elsewhere, and consumption people could no longer afford.
You cannot finance the same structural deficit out of savings forever.

### The way around the chokepoint got hit
The savings weren't the only thing holding. The routes that let oil pass around Hormuz were, too.
They are now under fire.
On September 10 and 11, drones struck Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, the 1,200-kilometer line that carries crude across the kingdom to Yanbu on the Red Sea, where tankers can load without going near Hormuz. Reuters reported that three pumping stations were damaged. Industry sources estimated five to six weeks for full repairs, with partial pumping potentially returning sooner.
The pipeline had been carrying roughly 4 to 5 million barrels a day.
That is **4 to 5% of the world 's oil supply -- roughly one barrel out of every 20 to 25 produced on Earth -- moving through one piece of infrastructure across Saudi Arabia.**
As of Monday, no crude loadings had been observed at Yanbu since September 16. Aramco has also halted or postponed some deliveries to European refiners, including contracted October supplies that should have been absolute baseline supply for Europe's energy systems.
Here is the part that would be funny if it weren't so expensive.
With the bypass around Hormuz damaged, Saudi Arabia has pushed more of its crude back out through **Hormuz** --the very chokepoint the bypass was built to avoid.
Saudi exports sank to about 2.4 million barrels a day in August, their lowest since at least 2013, and have rebounded above 4 million so far in September. Saudi crude is increasingly being carried out of the Persian Gulf and transferred to other tankers anchored off Oman--a ship-to-ship relay system that was unusual at anything like this scale before the war.
Those ship-to-ship transfers are now moving roughly 2.5 million barrels a day, up from 1.4 million in August: **an increase of almost 80% in one month.**
And moving the same barrel this way costs a lot, and consumes dramatically more infrastructure.
A normal supply chain is designed so a tanker loads, sails, unloads and goes somewhere else. In a shuttle system, ships spend more time repositioning, waiting, transferring cargo and making additional legs. Kpler estimates that moving 3 million barrels a day through these workarounds could require **36 to 40 additional VLCC (very large carrying capacity) supertankers** under its base case. Where do those ships come from? And if they're doing this, what else are they _not_ doing? (If transfers have to move farther away to Malaysia, the requirement could rise as high as 58.)
This is an important distinction in systems resilience: **a workaround can preserve capacity while destroying efficiency.** The oil may still arrive, but every barrel requires more ships, more crews, more insurance, more fuel, more time and more functioning pieces of infrastructure to get there.
That expense is showing up immediately. Freight on a supertanker carrying Gulf crude to China has climbed above **$30 per barrel** , by far the highest on record.
A barrel holds 42 gallons.
That means the tanker trip alone can now add the equivalent of roughly **71 cents per gallon of crude** _before_ the oil has been refined, piped inland, trucked anywhere, taxed or sold at a filling station.
A bypass does not make a chokepoint irrelevant... if destroying the bypass forces you back through the chokepoint.
I want to be careful describing Hormuz itself, because "closed" is the loose version and it is easy to knock down. The strait is a **severely constricted, militarized passage functioning through improvised exceptions,** some of them backed by the U.S. military. Visible traffic is a trickle. Kpler counted 17 commodity vessels crossing over the latest weekend, down from 37 the weekend before, while some Gulf tankers are believed to be moving with their transponders off.
That is not normal commerce.
It is not zero either.
The southern end of the Red Sea is in similar shape. Fifty-one vessels crossed the Bab el-Mandeb over the weekend, down from 57 the weekend before, so ships are still getting through. But Houthi attacks and related insecurity in the Red Sea had already helped cut exports from the Yanbu and Fujairah bypass ports from 7.8 million barrels a day in June to 5.5 million in August--a **29% retreat from the system 's emergency peak--before the Saudi pipeline itself was damaged.**
Call it what it is: two chokepoints that can no longer be counted on as ordinary commercial infrastructure.
Nor should anyone build a plan around a quick diplomatic fix. Iranian officials have publicly attached substantial political and security conditions to fully restoring navigation -- including but not limited to, the removal of both Trump and Netanyahu from executive power -- while American and Iranian officials have also signaled varying degrees of openness to renewed diplomacy.
Diplomacy may move quickly. It may not.
It hasn't been a reliable avenue for solving this problem so far.
A resilience plan that only works if diplomacy succeeds immediately is not much of a resilience plan.

### China: the shock absorber nobody voted for
One of the biggest shock absorbers of the last six months got almost no attention.
**China bought** _**half**_**the oil they usually do.**
Think of the physical oil market as an auction with a finite number of cargoes available today. China is normally the biggest bidder in the room. If the biggest bidder suddenly stops bidding on millions of barrels every day, everybody else gets breathing room to secure their own supply--even though no new oil was produced.
That is essentially what happened.
According to the IEA, Chinese seaborne crude imports fell from about 11.5 million barrels a day in February to near 6 million in June.
**China nearly halved its seaborne crude buying --a drop of about 48%.**
China could afford to reduce purchases because it entered the crisis with enormous stored inventories, built partly during the cheaper oil environment of 2025. Beijing also nearly shut down fuel exports in early March. It wasn't acting out of generosity. It was protecting its own economy.
But for everyone else, the systemic effect was the same as a gift: _millions of barrels a day that the world 's largest importer would ordinarily have been competing to buy were suddenly left on the table._
That is now changing.
Chinese customs data show total crude imports recovering from roughly 7.1 million barrels a day in June to 8.93 million in August--**about a 26% rebound in two months** --while still remaining 23% below a year earlier.
Its refineries processed 13.9 million barrels a day in August, up 11.2% from July and the highest rate since March. Beijing has eased fuel-export restrictions, allowing diesel and jet fuel to move back onto world markets.
The loose version of this story says China's reserves are gone.
They aren't.
China is still drawing substantial volumes from storage. Reuters estimated a draw of about 639,000 barrels a day in August, the second-largest monthly draw of the war.
What is changing is **how the cushion is being used.** China is running refineries harder, exporting fuel again and returning more actively to the crude market.
That is the number to pay attention to:
**The global market is this tight while China is still importing roughly a quarter less crude than it did a year ago.**
If Chinese purchasing continues toward normal levels, it does not create additional oil. It simply puts the largest bidder back into the auction for the same constrained pool of available cargoes.
The barrels China stops leaving on the table have to come from somewhere.

### From barrels to groceries
Crude is the number on the news.
Diesel is the number that reaches your groceries.
To understand why, it helps to know what a refinery actually does.
A refinery is not a big tank where crude goes in and whatever fuel society needs comes out. It is closer to an enormous, highly specialized industrial recipe. Different hydrocarbons boil, crack and react at different temperatures. The refinery's towers, catalytic crackers, hydrotreaters and other equipment are built to turn particular ranges of crude into particular mixtures of products.
An average 42-gallon barrel processed by a U.S. refinery yields roughly **19 to 20 gallons of gasoline, 11 to 13 gallons of distillate fuel such as diesel and heating oil, and 3 to 5 gallons of jet fuel** , plus a range of petrochemical feedstocks and other products. Refiners can shift that mix somewhat--but only within limits determined by the machinery they have and the chemistry of the crude going into it.
That's important because diesel and jet fuel are both middle distillates. A refinery can shift their production mix somewhat toward one or the other, but it cannot simply turn every spare barrel of gasoline into diesel because diesel happens to be scarce this month.
And not every crude oil is interchangeable. A refinery designed around particular grades of oil cannot necessarily substitute a radically different barrel without losing efficiency or changing equipment.
So "there is enough crude somewhere in the world" is not the same thing as "there is enough diesel where it is needed."
The physical chain looks more like this:
**Oil field -> tanker or pipeline -> refinery -> gasoline/diesel/jet fuel -> product storage -> pipeline/ship/truck -> local distributor -> end user.**
A bottleneck anywhere in that chain can create scarcity downstream even while the stage before it looks healthy.
You can have crude and not enough refinery capacity.
You can have refinery capacity and the wrong crude.
You can have diesel sitting at a coastal terminal and not enough functioning inland transport to put it into farm machinery three states away.
According to the IEA's September report, U.S. diesel prices passed the equivalent of $200 a barrel in early September, about **94% above pre-war levels**. _Almost doubling in eight months._ Gulf refiners exported only about a quarter as much diesel in August as before the war, while Russian refined-product exports have been hammered by attacks on refinery infrastructure and export restrictions.
Together, the Gulf and Russia are shipping roughly **1.6 million fewer barrels of diesel and gasoil every day than they did in February**. Before the war, those two sources supplied almost 45% of the world's seaborne diesel trade.
Refineries elsewhere are now being pushed hard to make up the difference.
And this is where the price of oil becomes the price of dinner.
Follow one loaf of bread backward.
Diesel runs machinery on the farm. Energy is embedded in fertilizer. Trucks bring seed, fertilizer and other inputs to the farm. Diesel powers harvest machinery. Another truck moves grain to an elevator. More transportation brings it to a mill. Processing consumes energy. Another truck moves flour or finished bread to a warehouse or distribution center. Another truck unloads at the grocery store.
**The price of diesel does not touch a loaf of bread once. It can touch the fertilizer, the tractor, the grain truck, the miller 's deliveries, the warehouse **_**and**_**the final truck to the supermarket.**
One energy shock can enter the cost of the same physical product at several different links in its journey.
And there is a **time lag.** A trucking company pays more for fuel today. A wholesaler sees higher freight bills next month. Contracts reset for next quarter. Farmers decide what they can afford to plant at planting time (and cannot make up the difference later). Processors alter prices. Retailers eventually pass some portion on to you--potentially with price gouging added on top at any link in the chain.
That is why the price shock at the pump can keep working its way into groceries **months** after the oil-market headline that started it has disappeared from the front page.
