Friend, Corporate money has no place in our politics ― at any level. But corporate PACs have been flooding our elections, seeking to ensure elected officials put corporate profits over the needs of our communities. And they’re empowered by the U.S. Supreme Court’s corruption and disastrous _Citizens United_ decision, as well as state laws that allow corporate donations to candidates. For example, cryptocurrency billionaires have spent more than $200 million trying to influence elections and legislation in Congress during this cycle alone. And in response to a massive defeat in the Senate last week on a bill written by the crypto industry, they plan to spend even more over the final weeks of this election. That’s why in Congress I have introduced and co-sponsored legislation such as the **_Protecting Our Democracy Act_** to hold elected officials accountable and get dark money out of politics, the **_DISCLOSE Act_** to require additional transparency in elections, the **_Democracy for All Amendment_** to overturn _Citizens United_ and limit corporate campaign spending while encouraging public campaign financing, and the **_Abolish Super PACs Act_**. With only six weeks until Election Day, now is the time to pressure Congress to advance these policies. **[Join me in demanding Congress act to get Big Money out of politics. Add your name to demand Congress pass legislation that stops billionaires, super PACs and corporations from attempting to drown out the voices of the people.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9osRFq5setnoPUPUKg2dRL5i2DWP84eBue997DK0S2CWCIynz1f3wdEJUxueaFYZHpp4iQZLXh-XGupwUT3ZlJO2LQRvP6Ew8hNCwu8_YucfhEcBFTYMiQlwkIJT8DuJgoG7D3XUVOynQMVl6uK-tlvAfFkI1SaUPeEELsQh3NEzU97phhqjr7GZ4flHP-IVuJMqtxOqgorx3c3Qg6Qh4go8GNRRRrGe7t0yo9fAg9cTEe6rKLDvCnnQxJ3Zotnhqbqc3NquY5_fwsskLeDW5PjNeankVD04LpbtF-wtrKlNGtGU7ZHH-HUYTFu1-5AGtUDak4wjwJoeeCbkEmyGCFA/4u9/XWAY7AGQRR-8EDXvXX77mw/h1/h001.yf4BIcZT3QKgxOw0WH3tmqRSAocQXhl1LgGUQ4HBuQ8)** [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9osRFq5setnoPUPUKg2dRL5i2DWP84eBue997DK0S2CWCIynz1f3wdEJUxueaFYZHrkLRa4hAtn5R5uqld_GYo9qfJmo0Cb6CaWqTXVAKkJLJERWkYWsaZ1PLY_XrpXDdKRalB1Mc3Vm504F_NZROEpsp3SsuIy7ue70QJ7A9djA2S_627RDQMNPp4F7TJXKXptBq6rDvme5nrM7r8IroNtB0x0BqJRna98K-VyzDnCjiCt-4a1I1KFXzleA6M8_h2Ff6tcc6kzj-gOTcZMXiiOzdchOOPzj9zsl62jVQUX5xdZn722TKx6YKbz_S7nj0pPlHXDLeGbzXGTm9Qqn8_A/4u9/XWAY7AGQRR-8EDXvXX77mw/h2/h001.ycuYQ7Miz9pTg4iJmVyMeRdUCB32646D8z-aukf9cB0) And in Michigan, the utility monopoly DTE Energy is spending millions of dollars to influence lawmakers. Fortunately, **this election, Michiganders have a chance to get corporate money out of our elections** by voting for a ballot measure that would ban utilities and corporations with state contracts over $250,000 from influencing elections. In addition to corporate PACs, we’re also taking on billionaire-funded PACs like **AIPAC and its affiliated PACs, which have once again spent more than $100 million in this year’s primary elections in an attempt to silence our movement and install more genocide-enablers in Congress.** This is the biggest source of Republican money interfering in Democratic elections, and AIPAC is spending more to influence this November’s general election. Together we’ve shown that people power can defeat a flood of special interest money with allies like Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Angie Nixon winning their Democratic primaries for U.S. Senate. Capital Rotation — September 22, 2026
Two Different Rallies, One Session, Neither Confirmed Yet
Oil's steepest drop this month and tech's best day in weeks both happened on the same session — for two different, unrelated reasons, both still unresolved.
|
---
| | What Moved
---|---
**Verified fact:** Monday was the market's best session in weeks — the S&P; 500 rose 1.06% to 7,731.78, the Nasdaq gained 1.65% to 26,961.08 on strength in technology and semiconductor names, and the Dow added 0.42% to 51,901.49. Crude fell 3.81% to $92.42, its steepest single-day drop this month, now well below the psychological $100 level breached just a session earlier.
| | Rotation Signal 01 — This Was a Convergence of Real Supply Data and Diplomatic Hope, Not Just One or the Other
---|---
**Verified fact:** Monday's oil decline was supported by confirmation that Saudi Arabia is restoring East-West Pipeline capacity and that crude exports have recovered from August lows, alongside renewed hope for Trump-Pezeshkian talks at the UN. **Our interpretation:** the combination of hard supply data and diplomatic sentiment moving in the same direction, on the same day, is a more durable basis for a price move than either alone — a notable contrast to earlier weeks when diplomatic headlines and physical shipping data repeatedly pointed in opposite directions.
| | Rotation Signal 02 — Technology Led on a Second, Unrelated Catalyst
---|---
**Verified fact:** technology and semiconductor stocks led Monday's gains, with Asian and European equities also advancing overnight, ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi summit addressing trade, rare earths, and AI cooperation. **Our interpretation:** this is the second consecutive session where the tech-sector rally appears connected to China-summit optimism rather than to the Iran/oil story — consistent with this newsletter's weekend finding that markets are now trading two genuinely separate regimes in parallel.
| | Rotation Signal 03 — The Rally Priced Optimism Ahead of Two Unresolved Events
---|---
**Current classification: PRESSURE, Priced as Resolving in Favor of Both Diplomatic Tracks.** Monday's gains across both energy-sensitive and technology-sensitive positioning reflect optimism ahead of events that have not yet occurred — a possible Trump-Pezeshkian meeting and Thursday's Trump-Xi summit. Both remain genuinely unresolved, and Trump's own UN remarks included rhetoric sharp enough to unwind Monday's oil move if followed by concrete escalation rather than talks.
| | What to Watch Today
---|---
Whether Tuesday's session holds Monday's gains as markets await concrete developments from the UN General Assembly, and whether technology names continue trading on China-summit optimism specifically rather than broader market sentiment.

Friends,

Out on the trail, I’m hearing more and more concern from constituents about the rising impact of data centers on our communities — concern that I very much share. **On Mike Lawler’s watch, five data centers have been built in Rockland County alone, with three more on the way.** In return, Rockland residents are left with higher utility bills and more uncertainty about how these projects may impact access to clean water and overall health. It’s no wonder these five data centers have been built here, given that **Mike Lawler is a former lobbyist for monopoly utility companies.** He has **taken hundreds of thousands from Big Tech** , and then turned around and **voted to give data center developers $80 billion in tax breaks while reducing restrictions on data center development.** Now, working families in the Hudson Valley are paying TWICE to subsidize the enormous amounts of energy that data centers use: once for the tax giveaway, and then a second time through higher household utility bills, which have risen by over 60%. **Mike Lawler had a choice, and he chose his donors over his district.** A choice he has made time and time again. During my time at the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) I worked on mitigating risk from emerging technology like AI and the CRITICAL role of government regulation. I know the urgency needed to meet this moment. We cannot blindly subsidize data centers. **We must fight for responsible regulations to make sure these companies don't pass utility costs onto families, hurt our environment, and exploit our communities.** While Mike Lawler spins blatant lies about me and my service, it is abundantly clear that Mike Lawler is in the pocket of the utility monopolies bankrolling his campaign. That’s who he’s fighting for. When I’m in Congress, I’ll be fighting for you.

With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

clean_body: | | | | Friends, Out on the trail, I’m hearing more and more concern from constituents about the rising impact of data centers on our communities — concern that I very much share. On Mike Lawler’s watch, five data centers have been built in Rockland County alone, with three more on the way. In return, Rockland residents are left with higher utility bills and more uncertainty about how these projects may impact access to clean water and overall health. It’s no wonder these five data centers have been built here, given that Mike Lawler is a former lobbyist for monopoly utility companies. He has taken hundreds of thousands from Big Tech , and then turned around and voted to give data center developers $80 billion in tax breaks while reducing restrictions on data center development. Now, working families in the Hudson Valley are paying TWICE to subsidize the enormous amounts of energy that data centers use: once for the tax giveaway, and then a second time through higher household utility bills, which have risen by over 60%. Mike Lawler had a choice, and he chose his donors over his district. A choice he has made time and time again. During my time at the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) I worked on mitigating risk from emerging technology like AI and the CRITICAL role of government regulation. I know the urgency needed to meet this moment. We cannot blindly subsidize data centers. We must fight for responsible regulations to make sure these companies don't pass utility costs onto families, hurt our environment, and exploit our communities. While Mike Lawler spins blatant lies about me and my service, it is abundantly clear that Mike Lawler is in the pocket of the utility monopolies bankrolling his campaign. That’s who he’s fighting for. When I’m in Congress, I’ll be fighting for you. | | | Rep. John McGuire would like to tell you that the war in Iran has “nothing” to do with the insane, skyrocketing gas and diesel prices. ** ** And it’s _not_ Donald Trump’s unnecessary and illegal war of choice that’s driving up costs at the pump, in the grocery stores, and even our interest rates._According to McGuire, it’s actually Joe Biden’s fault_. ** ** Let’s look at what has actually happened since the start of this war: The average price of gasoline has risen 45%, and diesel is up 66%. ** ** The Congressional Budget Office – the nonpartisan federal agency that provides economic data and analysis to members of Congress – has explicitly said that**the war is responsible for the spike**. And independent economists across the spectrum have reached the same conclusion that anyone with common sense reached the day Trump first bombed Iran. ** ** The price tag of the war itself tells an identical story. Earlier this month, it was estimated that this war has cost the U.S. $43 billion, but when you factor in the massive economic burden on American consumers, that total rises to _$100 billion. _** ** Why can’t McGuire just be honest about what is obvious to everyone else? ** ** **It’s because his loyalty is not to the people who he is supposed to serve. It is not to the truth. And it sure isn’t to common sense. His loyalty is to one man, even if that costs him his last shred of credibility.** ** ** This is the same guy who voted for the Big Ugly Bill that experts knew would wreak havoc on the middle class and clinics across the district. He voted for a war that Trump had promised America he would not start. ** ** He’s so ride-or-die for Donald Trump that he is willing to lie to our faces (or just avoid us entirely!) and tell us that this war he keeps voting to fund – the one that’s draining our wallets, threatening our safety, killing civilians abroad, and destroying our nation’s reputation – has nothing to do with our increased costs. Whatever the cost to the people of this district, McGuire will sign off, as long as Trump is happy. ** ** Folks around here are being crushed by the costs of Washington’s corruption and cruelty, and while they don’t expect Congress to solve every problem, they have every right to a representative who won’t make everything worse. ** **_McGuire has failed both tests. clean_body: Friend, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. Peter,I believe Democrats can actually win power back. Not through one big moment, but by organizing and winning races that may not always be in the spotlight.Wisconsin's 7th District is exactly that kind of race. Republicans have held this seat for 16 years. It's rated as one of the toughest districts in the country for Democrats to flip. But tough doesn’t mean impossible. The path to flipping the House runs through races where organizing makes the difference, and WI-07 is one of them. **Fred Clark is already doing the hard work of organizing this very tough district.** He’s visited all 26 counties, talking to voters of all stripes about healthcare, the cost of diesel, and childcare. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM5NzM0OTUS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU0MDQ4NTQwMQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
There are less than 50 days before November’s midterm elections. The path to an environmental majority in the Senate relies on winning in
Michigan and Ohio.

Recent polls show that if the election were held tomorrow, Republicans would be favored to keep control of the Senate.

We need your help before the FEC close-of-books deadline on September 30. Please, donate today >> https://links.messages.lcv. Peter — we're reaching out today because the situation in Michigan and
Ohio is truly urgent. Both of these Senate races have a climate championfacing off against a member of the Dirty Dozen — our list of the worst
anti-environment candidates of the cycle. Each race is a true toss-up that will be decided by a tiny number of votes. ... and in these races, we have game-changing research showing a huge number of swing voters who haven't decided yet. We can't afford to lose these states. So we're asking: Please, rush your urgent contribution of $15 or more today to help elect climate champions and win the Senate in November >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/Zzb0Mqe_ DONATE TODAY >> https://links.messages.lcv. We have a real shot at winning these races and taking back a majority in the
Senate — but we need your help. ❌ That means beating Mike Rogers in Michigan.Rogers has built his political career off of dirty money from Big Oil and Big
Tech — he’s taken roughly $693,000 in direct contributions from oil and gas
industry donors alone. This is a race we can win, but only with your support. Please pitch in $15 or more today >> https://links.messages.lcv. ❌It means going up against Jon Husted in Ohio. The state went heavily for Trump,
but Husted has become the corrupt "face of data centers" — even as Ohioans face
skyrocketing energy costs. This is a tight raceand it’s one we urgently need to win in November to regain control of the
Senate. Please, make your contribution of $15 or more today to help us take on Husted >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/9zEZMdG9qEF_ Our best-in-class door-to-door canvassing and paid media programs — combining
persuasion and turnout efforts — have helped deliver decisive margins in close
races for the last decade through an effective mix of digital, TV, mail, and
field tactics. We also have expertise running vote-by-mail and early voting programs, including
“chasing” voters to return their ballots and communicating with them about
voting options in their states. But the real game changer is this: Our research has shown that 42% of swing voters are “very concerned” about
rising electricity bills, and that our messaging — focused on lowering costs
with clean energy — moves them 7% toward supporting environmental champions in
November. These “energy bill voters” will be decisive in close races this fall. We have a strategy to turn out these voters, but right now, our campaigns are
still underfunded. This moment is critical not just for November’s midterm elections, but for the
future of our climate and democracy. Whether it’s blocking or repealing clean energy projects, providing handouts to
dirty and expensive fuels like oil, coal, and gas, or embracing costly data
center buildouts — these are candidates who have consistently sided with Big Polluters over people. Can we count on you to chip in $15 or more today to help us take back the Senate in November? https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/L6b_ Thank you for everything you do for people and the planet, Peter. A lot of people will be watching:
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=99%2E42639%2EujeBEx)
In just a moment, I am going to ask you to make a contribution to my re-election campaign to Congress in Pennsylvania. Please give me a chance to explain why this request – especially today – is so important.
In just a few days, we close the books on our final quarterly FEC fundraising deadline of this campaign. And when it ends, we're legally required to report what we've raised. The number of donations we've received will also be public.
A lot of people will be watching:
National Republicans will be watching. As the last Democrat in Pennsylvania who represents a battleground seat, our opponents will be taking stock of whether or not they have a chance to flip this seat by spending large amounts of money to beat us. I'd prefer they did not.
The press will be watching. Not only for the same reasons, but the truth is they'll probably be looking to see the grassroots strength of our campaign given all the 'will I or won't I run against Fetterman' questions I've been getting.
If we report a big number, Republicans will stay away and we can lock down this seat - making it more likely Democrats take back the House. Plus, for better or worse, every donation kind of sends a message about the desire for a strong challenge to John Fetterman when this election ends.
So this is a big deal. And I am hoping for a huge number of individual donations before this deadline ends. Especially from Pennsylvanians.

_And_ that means turning out eligible voters across the Commonwealth. If we do that, we can win competitive races that could determine control of Congress – and we can send such a strong message about where Virginia – and the country – stands.

Winning this race, electing Virginia Democrats, and turning voters out is the goal of my campaign over the next six weeks – and I’m relying on grassroots donors like you to ensure we have the resources required to do that critical work.

# **A third of Democrats say they 'd be happy if Trump was assassinated: poll**
A Center for Strategic Politics **[survey of 683 Democratic voters](https://substack.com/redirect/19f48013-c396-473b-92a3-c599007c42e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** found large majorities favoring Trump's removal via impeachment (87%) or the 25th Amendment (84%), while many said they'd feel positive about the removal of Trump via a military coup (59%) or Trump dying of natural causes (55%).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19f48013-c396-473b-92a3-c599007c42e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Roughly a third of respondents said they 'd feel positive if Trump were assassinated at a rally,** while 43% said they'd feel negative and a quarter said they'd be neutral.
* **The poll also found strong Democratic support for prosecuting Trump administration officials** over immigration enforcement, the Iran war, and drug-boat strikes, along with backing for expanding the Supreme Court and ending the Senate filibuster -- as House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has left open the possibility of a third impeachment attempt.

* * *
# **Trump touts American strength, predicts Iran deal in UN speech**
President Donald Trump addressed the UN General Assembly, Tuesday, emphasizing U.S. leadership in AI, which he rebranded to "superintelligence," and predicted Iran would strike a deal with Washington after November's midterms, arguing military action had prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon while calling for allies to join a full economic isolation of Iran.

subject: Obama’s legacy still undermines our elections
body:
[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=3e0bcbfa07ee44a2a5752eb56bc10e82&_e=aZ8cdLQx9CdMTJ0WQ-XnjsyPHqXo3HdZhXe4MkkSNdu6Pjtz-glvIxQ8bH_Z3J--KivM5qBU1qgjgKY_P7F0IL9AMj0oi0uGfy1gwkC7MVeWzKNkH6yNuLT6g-WdaE6BJtIR3Vt5IYtylbmSdBvh5WNJB3lHRznDBd-jg5f9NlQEEyIppuCGMtV891jZkIgA5ooZDkFZnTyOdVLotQZjStGm1VPPYD7gX4Izo-G_VjWdPciD8VZO2RseNNt-soQao4cyeBfsgTrBzHO1rVfOquS4ebddYSofS_6hXqUoQ-HAyepghfWcCUiIU_cCbhtVXGsD-o0QVQDwSQOTQzIbRK2fl_0csgO-5lf6ABreIa9Rhm600U-4Qd-eiss4w6l2XZwbNWl2hJ-Usoesil76y-TuD6_C0kxh3G3PH_okuOnopi3W9-dLSgTHUB5hh8T7vbPQyso1n4V0xbvgiQSdB32_WpXT1aeF2b6xguPyzJva_-RMeaCbv-dX5LEXSuq0XcUJwnLBpeVibWt3Ey92yfBXgs15L5J5N31RvqjGj49n4Ddzx-jmS3LgeLhLKVPjie8_Z6ToVHMKY-0MJ8ckBmG_WEe38XHh38mz3lowr1Do0GVdDpj0OhKfrERz_OdwrIXXWdYuPuUQoHi546jmHA%3D%3D)

Friend,

Back in 2008, Barack Obama promised the American people he would _" fundamentally change America."_ He meant every word. Look at what has happened to our election laws since that promise.

**Consider what states across the country have done in the years since that promise.**
* Voter ID requirements have been weakened or eliminated in states that once required them.
* Ballot harvesting, once illegal almost everywhere, is now permitted in a growing number of states.
* Deadlines for counting votes have stretched so long that "election night" barely means anything anymore.

This erosion took nearly twenty years to unfold, but the damage it has done to our elections has been enormous.

Landmark Legal Foundation has been in this fight for decades, defending the Constitution in courtrooms across the country long before election integrity became a headline issue.

**And Landmark Legal Foundation continues to fight Obama 's terrible changes, case by case, court by court. **

That's why I'm asking every one of our supporters to help me raise $750,000 this year to keep this work moving, and I'm asking you to be part of it right now.

Please donate $10, $35, $250, or whatever amount you're able to give today.

[Support Landmark Legal Foundation](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=3e0bcbfa07ee44a2a5752eb56bc10e82&_e=aZ8cdLQx9CdMTJ0WQ-XnjsyPHqXo3HdZhXe4MkkSNdu6Pjtz-glvIxQ8bH_Z3J--KivM5qBU1qgjgKY_P7F0IL9AMj0oi0uGfy1gwkC7MVeWzKNkH6yNuLT6g-WdaE6BJtIR3Vt5IYtylbmSdBvh5WNJB3lHRznDBd-jg5f9NlQrmKQNOAwTm0FHVUpdPddBqU-gDMFfvWfj5KQWzY5LZc0EBHbD_uePPhQPqqJ9UbLClhq1iUn78ACB5gxwU75uoUzO08mN2Ho3HG3yKzeqpwuhmF7cDO1TEZz6mr5oSkZGFw7CF8wAUZqnRkUty2rhi2QlC_52oYNyYg-1LPDvh7Cr8_BqDXA5XODKi_v4jyjstii7HadBAbAo9xQdFsmEePq3kRWecO851-MnqLrSMgvYvNUgV4vFmZrWdELqzgb2aZejnH8Cxao-1uAMYZamvX1QC8z_Jw9fzojrHxwzb9Dc_BoyXZFrTPwxcoHywh-U3hD_oVcxbxuOXaGHRVxIR2Fg-vQjMOK-8q3DyEwLP0ZxFYMG6cwNLCLjKvWWkmCZInOsXJs8l-L5ILz5PS_Xuv8kSlzdVPoXcYfOlOUND_YKTAV7BRDzbXQJyZ6mWq9V01uioGG37QKPS-bEbm0e5m9JPt0byIhB5_ka5DFTIKfO10DbgreD_C6G6JK4z9E%3D)

Here's what makes Landmark's approach different from most conservative organizations working on election integrity today.

**Defending Election Integrity**
In _Brnovich v. Democratic National Committee_ , Landmark helped win a critical Supreme Court victory defending an Arizona law that placed commonsense restrictions on ballot harvesting.

Arizona's legislature had passed the law to protect the chain of custody for mailed ballots, and opponents sued to strike it down.

clean_body: Friend, Back in 2008, Barack Obama promised the American people he would " fundamentally change America." He meant every word. Look at what has happened to our election laws since that promise. Consider what states across the country have done in the years since that promise. Voter ID requirements have been weakened or eliminated in states that once required them. Ballot harvesting, once illegal almost everywhere, is now permitted in a growing number of states. Deadlines for counting votes have stretched so long that "election night" barely means anything anymore. This erosion took nearly twenty years to unfold, but the damage it has done to our elections has been enormous. Landmark Legal Foundation has been in this fight for decades, defending the Constitution in courtrooms across the country long before election integrity became a headline issue. And Landmark Legal Foundation continues to fight Obama 's terrible changes, case by case, court by court. That's why I'm asking every one of our supporters to help me raise $750,000 this year to keep this work moving, and I'm asking you to be part of it right now. Please donate $10, $35, $250, or whatever amount you're able to give today. Here's what makes Landmark's approach different from most conservative organizations working on election integrity today. Defending Election Integrity In Brnovich v. Democratic National Committee , Landmark helped win a critical Supreme Court victory defending an Arizona law that placed commonsense restrictions on ballot harvesting. Arizona's legislature had passed the law to protect the chain of custody for mailed ballots, and opponents sued to strike it down. Landmark filed a brief defending Arizona 's authority to secure its own elections, and the Supreme Court agreed, upholding the law and confirming that states have wide latitude to protect against fraud. That ruling now stands as precedent for every state considering similar election security laws. - Fighting Lawfare in the Courts When the Colorado Supreme Court tried to strike Donald Trump from the 2024 ballot by stretching a 14th Amendment provision written for insurrectionists, Landmark fought back at the U.S. Supreme Court. The justices ruled 9-0 that Colorado had no authority to make that call, protecting every voter 's right to choose their own president. Landmark took on a similar fight when Special Counsel Jack Smith brought charges against President Trump. Our team argued that Smith's appointment violated the Constitution because the Senate never confirmed him to that office. Judge Aileen Cannon agreed, and the charges were dismissed entirely. Both cases protect the same principle. Voters decide who leads this country, and no court or unconfirmed official gets to override that choice.** Landmark needs your help today. Please select an amount below to help us reach our $750,000 goal this year. Thank you for standing with us, and for taking the time to read this whole email. Richard "Pete" Hutchison President & General Counsel Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

Hey Peter, Cait here. This email isn’t going out to everyone tonight. It’s just going to a select crew of folks like you that we have been hoping to convince to make an online donation to our campaign*. I need to ask a favor, and I’m hoping you’re someone who can help. In a little over a week, our campaign has our final quarterly FEC deadline of the election, when we publicly release data on how much we’ve raised and from how many donors. NY-17 is going to be the most competitive and expensive House race in the country. Donald Trump is spending millions on ads here. So it’s really important that we be able to put out a strong report that shows we’re on track to push back on the dark money and beat Mike Lawler. People are going to be looking to gauge the strength of our campaign, and we cannot afford to come up short of our goals. That’s why I’m turning to you. name: Public Land Warriors
subject: Why Trump is moving the Forest Service
body:
This is a purge, plain and simple
This is a purge, plain and simple

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/zaqGXMFZQCsKJEF23fkzQQ~~/AAUS1hA~/BThrnCpQ2VTyhCduebcTHj0ol1KxnmnhkCMHRbzxKgHrsDnF89khkZp53usznAZ7-eLp5uu8NYUMLRZOikT64aYIBW1ff-YWyJUhnoV37llCp1EVOVvvuYZMcq_YNnAf)
| | | | Peter, Let’s talk about why this government decided to uproot the U.S. Forest Service headquarters from Washington, D.C., and relocate it to Utah. The politicians pushing this are blanketing the airwaves with a convenient talking point: this is just about "bringing leadership closer to where the work happens." But that’s false. We know exactly what the strategy is here because we watched them run the exact same playbook in 2020. When the Bureau of Land Management headquarters was scattered out West, **almost 90% of the employees ordered to relocate chose to resign rather than uproot their families.** It stripped the agency of decades of institutional knowledge and effectively crippled it—which was precisely the point. The newest attack on the Forest Service goes even further. By moving headquarters, they are shuttering dozens of critical research centers and closing regional offices right before what is predicted to be a horrific wildfire season. Severing the Forest Service from the seat of power in Washington is a deliberate move to blindfold and bankrupt the agency. Over the last year, roughly a quarter of the Forest Service's 30,000 employees were already coerced or forced out. Now, thousands more are being handed relocation orders. If the BLM history is any guide, the Forest Service will soon be left with roughly half of its former ranks. As a result of this purge, campgrounds will close, trails will crumble, high fuel loads near communities will go unaddressed—making wildfires infinitely harder to fight. And when things inevitably start going wrong on the ground, the politicians who manufactured this crisis will throw up their hands, declare the federal government incompetent, and demand these public lands be sold off to private industry. **And just in case there was any doubt about their end game, look at where they are moving the agency: Utah.** They chose the home turf of Senator Mike Lee—the loudest architect of the public land selloff—and a state that is actively suing the federal government to take over millions of acres of your public lands. It is a bleak picture, but here is the good news: the inevitable does not need to happen. Because they are being so blatant about this corporate land grab, they are handing us the ammunition we need to stop them. The only thing that can prevent our forests from being mismanaged to the point of a fire sale is the organized, overwhelming outrage of the American people. [**We need to blanket the airwaves, expose this engineered collapse, and make supporting this purge politically toxic.
